alex_tab_size :: Int
alex_base :: AlexAddr
alex_table :: AlexAddr

alex_action_3 :: Posn -> Text -> Token
alex_action_4 :: Posn -> Text -> Token
alex_action_5 :: Posn -> Text -> Token
alex_action_6 :: Posn -> Text -> Token
alex_action_7 :: Posn -> Text -> Token
data AlexAddr
AlexA# :: Addr# -> AlexAddr
alexIndexInt16OffAddr :: AlexAddr -> Int# -> Int#
alexIndexInt32OffAddr :: AlexAddr -> Int# -> Int#
quickIndex :: Array Int (AlexAcc (ZonkAny 0 :: Type)) -> Int -> AlexAcc (ZonkAny 0 :: Type)
data AlexReturn a
AlexEOF :: AlexReturn a
AlexError :: !AlexInput -> AlexReturn a
AlexSkip :: !AlexInput -> !Int -> AlexReturn a
AlexToken :: !AlexInput -> !Int -> a -> AlexReturn a
alexScan :: (Posn, Char, [Byte], Text) -> Int -> AlexReturn (Posn -> Text -> Token)
alexScanUser :: t -> (Posn, Char, [Byte], Text) -> Int -> AlexReturn (Posn -> Text -> Token)
alex_scan_tkn :: t1 -> t2 -> Int# -> AlexInput -> Int# -> AlexLastAcc -> (AlexLastAcc, AlexInput)
data AlexLastAcc
AlexNone :: AlexLastAcc
AlexLastAcc :: !Int -> !AlexInput -> !Int -> AlexLastAcc
AlexLastSkip :: !AlexInput -> !Int -> AlexLastAcc
data AlexAcc user
AlexAccNone :: AlexAcc user
AlexAcc :: Int -> AlexAcc user
AlexAccSkip :: AlexAcc user

-- | Create a token with position.
tok :: (Text -> Tok) -> Posn -> Text -> Token

-- | Token without position.
data Tok

-- | Reserved word or symbol.
TK :: {-# UNPACK #-} !TokSymbol -> Tok

-- | String literal.
TL :: !Text -> Tok

-- | Integer literal.
TI :: !Text -> Tok

-- | Identifier.
TV :: !Text -> Tok

-- | Float literal.
TD :: !Text -> Tok

-- | Character literal.
TC :: !Text -> Tok
T_VarIdentToken :: !Text -> Tok
T_HoleIdentToken :: !Text -> Tok

-- | Smart constructor for <a>Tok</a> for the sake of backwards
--   compatibility.
pattern TS :: Text -> Int -> Tok

-- | Keyword or symbol tokens have a unique ID.
data TokSymbol
TokSymbol :: Text -> !Int -> TokSymbol

-- | Keyword or symbol text.
[tsText] :: TokSymbol -> Text

-- | Unique ID.
[tsID] :: TokSymbol -> !Int

-- | Token with position.
data Token
PT :: Posn -> Tok -> Token
Err :: Posn -> Token

-- | Pretty print a position.
printPosn :: Posn -> String

-- | Pretty print the position of the first token in the list.
tokenPos :: [Token] -> String

-- | Get the position of a token.
tokenPosn :: Token -> Posn

-- | Get line and column of a token.
tokenLineCol :: Token -> (Int, Int)

-- | Get line and column of a position.
posLineCol :: Posn -> (Int, Int)

-- | Convert a token into "position token" form.
mkPosToken :: Token -> ((Int, Int), Text)

-- | Convert a token to its text.
tokenText :: Token -> Text

-- | Convert a token to a string.
prToken :: Token -> String

-- | Finite map from text to token organized as binary search tree.
data BTree

-- | Nil (leaf).
N :: BTree

-- | Binary node.
B :: Text -> Tok -> BTree -> BTree -> BTree

-- | Convert potential keyword into token or use fallback conversion.
eitherResIdent :: (Text -> Tok) -> Text -> Tok

-- | The keywords and symbols of the language organized as binary search
--   tree.
resWords :: BTree

-- | Unquote string literal.
unescapeInitTail :: Text -> Text
data Posn
Pn :: !Int -> !Int -> !Int -> Posn
alexStartPos :: Posn
alexMove :: Posn -> Char -> Posn
type Byte = Word8
type AlexInput = (Posn, Char, [Byte], Text)
tokens :: Text -> [Token]
alexGetByte :: AlexInput -> Maybe (Byte, AlexInput)
alexInputPrevChar :: AlexInput -> Char

-- | Encode a Haskell String to a list of Word8 values, in UTF8 format.
utf8Encode :: Char -> [Word8]
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.Syntax.Lex.Posn
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.Syntax.Lex.Tok
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.Syntax.Lex.TokSymbol
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.Syntax.Lex.Token
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Language.Rzk.Syntax.Lex.Posn
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Language.Rzk.Syntax.Lex.Tok
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Language.Rzk.Syntax.Lex.TokSymbol
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Language.Rzk.Syntax.Lex.Token
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.Syntax.Lex.BTree
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.Syntax.Lex.Posn
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.Syntax.Lex.Tok
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.Syntax.Lex.TokSymbol
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.Syntax.Lex.Token

module Language.Rzk.Syntax.Layout
data LayoutDelimiters
LayoutDelimiters :: TokSymbol -> Maybe TokSymbol -> Maybe TokSymbol -> LayoutDelimiters
[delimSep] :: LayoutDelimiters -> TokSymbol

-- | Nothing for toplevel layout.
[delimOpen] :: LayoutDelimiters -> Maybe TokSymbol

-- | Nothing for toplevel layout.
[delimClose] :: LayoutDelimiters -> Maybe TokSymbol
layoutWords :: [(TokSymbol, LayoutDelimiters)]
layoutStopWords :: [TokSymbol]
layoutOpen :: [TokSymbol]
layoutClose :: [TokSymbol]
layoutSep :: [TokSymbol]
parenOpen :: [TokSymbol]
parenClose :: [TokSymbol]

-- | Report an error during layout resolution.
layoutError :: [Token] -> String -> a

-- | Replace layout syntax with explicit layout tokens.
resolveLayout :: Bool -> [Token] -> [Token]
type Position = Posn
type Line = Int
type Column = Int

-- | Entry of the layout stack.
data Block

-- | An implicit layout block with its start column.
Implicit :: LayoutDelimiters -> Status -> Column -> Block
Explicit :: Block

-- | Get current indentation. 0 if we are in an explicit block.
indentation :: Block -> Column

-- | Check if s block is implicit.
isImplicit :: Block -> Bool
data Status

-- | A layout column that has not been confirmed by a line break
Tentative :: Status

-- | A layout column that has been confirmed by a line break.
Definitive :: Status

-- | Add a new implicit layout block.
addImplicit :: LayoutDelimiters -> Position -> Position -> [Block] -> [Block]

-- | Confirm tentative blocks that are not more indented than <tt>col</tt>.
confirm :: Column -> [Block] -> [Block]

-- | Get the position immediately to the right of the given token. If no
--   token is given, gets the first position in the file.
afterPrev :: Maybe Token -> Position

-- | Get the position immediately to the right of the given token.
nextPos :: Token -> Position

-- | Get the number of characters in the token.
tokenLength :: Token -> Int

-- | Create a position symbol token.
sToken :: Position -> TokSymbol -> Token

-- | Get the line number of a token.
line :: Token -> Line

-- | Get the column number of a token.
column :: Token -> Column

-- | Is the following token on a new line?
newLine :: Maybe Token -> Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a word is a layout start token.
isLayout :: Token -> Maybe LayoutDelimiters

-- | Check if a token is one of the given symbols.
isTokenIn :: [TokSymbol] -> Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a token is a layout stop token.
isStop :: Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a token is the layout open token.
isLayoutOpen :: Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a token is the layout separator token.
isLayoutSep :: Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a token is the layout close token.
isLayoutClose :: Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a token is an opening parenthesis.
isParenOpen :: Token -> Bool

-- | Check if a token is a closing parenthesis.
isParenClose :: Token -> Bool

module Language.Rzk.Syntax
parseModuleSafe :: Text -> IO (Either Text Module)
parseModule :: Text -> Either Text Module
parseModuleRzk :: Text -> Either Text Module
parseModuleFile :: FilePath -> IO (Either Text Module)

-- | Replace layout syntax with explicit layout tokens.
resolveLayout :: Bool -> [Token] -> Either String [Token]

-- | The printer class does the job.
class Print a
prt :: Print a => Int -> a -> Doc

-- | Like <a>printTree</a>, but does not insert newlines for curly braces.
printTree :: Print a => a -> String
tryExtractMarkdownCodeBlocks :: Text -> Text -> Text

-- | Extract code for a given alias (e.g. "rzk" or "haskell") from a
--   Markdown file by replacing any lines that do not belong to the code in
--   that language with blank lines. This way the line numbers are
--   preserved correctly from the original file.
--   
--   All of the following notations are supported to start a code block:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><pre>```rzk</pre></li>
--   <li><pre>```{.rzk title="Example"}</pre></li>
--   <li><pre>``` { .rzk title="Example" }</pre></li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; example = "Example:\n```rzk\n#lang rzk-1\n```\nasd asd\n```rzk\n#def x : U\n  := U\n``` \nasda"
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; putStrLn example
--   Example:
--   ```rzk
--   #lang rzk-1
--   ```
--   asd asd
--   ```rzk
--   #def x : U
--     := U
--   ```
--   asda
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; putStrLn $ T.unpack $ extractMarkdownCodeBlocks "rzk" example
--   
--   
--   #lang rzk-1
--   
--   
--   
--   #def x : U
--     := U
--   </pre>
extractMarkdownCodeBlocks :: Text -> Text -> Text
tryOrDisplayException :: Either Text a -> IO (Either Text a)
tryOrDisplayExceptionIO :: IO (Either Text a) -> IO (Either Text a)


-- | Surface names, binders and modalities.
--   
--   These are what the checker shows the user, and they are independent of
--   how a term represents its variables: a <a>VarIdent</a> is a surface
--   identifier (with the position of its defining occurrence), and a
--   <a>Binder</a> records the <i>names</i> a binder introduces — including
--   a pair pattern, which still binds exactly one variable whose
--   components are projections of it.
module Language.Rzk.Foil.Names

-- | An identifier that is not in scope becomes a hole under a
--   <i>marked</i> name.
--   
--   A free-foil term refers to a variable by name, and an unresolved
--   identifier has none — so the term cannot represent it. Elaboration
--   marks it instead, and the checker reports it when it reaches it, which
--   is what keeps the error where the identifier was used (inside the
--   binders and topes it was written under) rather than at the top of the
--   declaration.
--   
--   The marker cannot be mistaken for a hole the user wrote: the grammar
--   forbids <tt>#</tt> in an identifier.
markUnresolved :: VarIdent -> VarIdent
unmarkUnresolved :: VarIdent -> Maybe VarIdent

-- | What a bound name is shown as: the display name standing for the
--   variable itself, and the (freshened) binder, which gives the pattern
--   to print and the component names to fold projections back to.
type Display = (VarIdent, Binder)

-- | The annotation on every node of a typed term: its type, plus its
--   memoised weak head and normal forms.
data TypeInfo term
TypeInfo :: term -> Maybe term -> Maybe term -> TypeInfo term
[infoType] :: TypeInfo term -> term
[infoWHNF] :: TypeInfo term -> Maybe term
[infoNF] :: TypeInfo term -> Maybe term
data RzkPosition
RzkPosition :: Maybe FilePath -> BNFC'Position -> RzkPosition
[rzkFilePath] :: RzkPosition -> Maybe FilePath
[rzkLineCol] :: RzkPosition -> BNFC'Position
ppRzkPosition :: RzkPosition -> String
newtype VarIdent
VarIdent :: VarIdent' RzkPosition -> VarIdent
[getVarIdent] :: VarIdent -> VarIdent' RzkPosition
ppVarIdentWithLocation :: VarIdent -> String
varIdent :: VarIdent -> VarIdent
varIdentAt :: Maybe FilePath -> VarIdent -> VarIdent
fromVarIdent :: VarIdent -> VarIdent

-- | The display name of a hole from its surface token text. The token
--   includes the leading <tt>?</tt>; an anonymous hole (bare <tt>?</tt>)
--   has no name.
holeName :: Text -> Maybe VarIdent

-- | The surface token text (including the leading <tt>?</tt>) for a hole
--   name.
holeIdentToken :: Maybe VarIdent -> Text

-- | The name(s) a binder introduces. A binder may name a single (possibly
--   anonymous) variable, or destructure a pair/tuple via a pattern. The
--   pattern structure is kept around purely so that goals, holes and error
--   messages can show the user's original names (e.g. <tt>t</tt> and
--   <tt>s</tt> for <tt>\ (t , s) -&gt; …</tt>) instead of projections of a
--   fresh variable (e.g. <tt>π₁ x₄</tt> and <tt>π₂ x₄</tt>).
--   
--   Operationally a pair pattern still binds a <i>single</i> variable; the
--   components are projections of it (see <tt>toScopePattern</tt>).
--   <a>Binder</a> only records the names so they can be restored when
--   rendering.
data Binder

-- | a single variable (<tt>Nothing</tt> for <tt>_</tt>)
BinderVar :: Maybe VarIdent -> Binder

-- | a pair pattern <tt>(l , r)</tt>
BinderPair :: Binder -> Binder -> Binder

-- | the unit pattern <tt>unit</tt>
BinderUnit :: Binder

-- | The single name of a binder, if it binds exactly one named variable. A
--   pair/unit pattern has no single name, so this is <a>Nothing</a> for
--   them. Used wherever the old <tt>Maybe VarIdent</tt> binder name is
--   still sufficient.
binderName :: Binder -> Maybe VarIdent
data TModality
Sharp :: TModality
Flat :: TModality
Op :: TModality
Id :: TModality
toModality :: Modality -> TModality
fromMod :: TModality -> Modality

-- | A tuple pattern is sugar for nested pairs.
desugarTuple :: BNFC'Position -> [Pattern] -> Pattern -> Pattern -> Pattern
toBinder :: Pattern -> Binder
patternToTerm :: Pattern -> Term
modalColonModality :: ModalColon -> Modality
modalColonToTModality :: ModalColon -> TModality
fromTModalityToModalColon :: TModality -> ModalColon

-- | Split a binder term into the individual variables it names. A
--   multi-variable binder like <tt>(x y : A)</tt> is parsed as the
--   application spine <tt>x y</tt>; this returns <tt>[x, y]</tt> so each
--   can become its own nested binder. A single binder term (a variable, a
--   pair pattern, …) is returned unchanged as a singleton.
flattenBinderApp :: Term -> [Term]
unsafeTermToPattern :: Term -> Pattern
sigmaParamToTypeSigma :: BNFC'Position -> SigmaParam -> Term -> Term

-- | A projection step: first (<tt>π₁</tt>) or second (<tt>π₂</tt>)
--   component.
data Proj
PFst :: Proj
PSnd :: Proj

-- | Render a <a>Binder</a> as a surface pattern (used to display the
--   binder itself, e.g. <tt>(t , s)</tt>). Anonymous variables become
--   <tt>_</tt>.
binderToPattern :: Binder -> Pattern

-- | A <a>VarIdent</a> that prints as the binder's surface pattern, e.g.
--   <tt>(t , s)</tt>. Used to display a pattern binder in a hole's local
--   context as the pattern itself rather than as the underlying single
--   variable.
binderDisplayName :: Binder -> VarIdent

-- | The named leaves of a binder, each paired with the projection path
--   that reaches it from the bound variable. For example <tt>(t , (a ,
--   b))</tt> yields <tt>[([PFst], t), ([PSnd, PFst], a), ([PSnd, PSnd],
--   b)]</tt>.
binderPaths :: Binder -> [([Proj], VarIdent)]

-- | The names appearing in a binder.
binderLeaves :: Binder -> [VarIdent]

-- | Does this binder destructure a pair/tuple (as opposed to naming a
--   single variable or <tt>_</tt>)?
binderIsCompound :: Binder -> Bool

-- | Refresh the named leaves of a binder so they avoid the given names
--   (and one another). Anonymous leaves and the unit pattern are left
--   unchanged.
freshenBinderLeaves :: [VarIdent] -> Binder -> Binder

-- | Decompose a chain of projections applied to a variable into the
--   projection path <i>from the variable outwards</i>, matching
--   <a>binderPaths</a>. The outermost projection is applied last, so it
--   goes at the <i>end</i> of the path: e.g. <tt>π₂ (π₁ x)</tt> (select
--   <tt>π₁</tt> first, then <tt>π₂</tt>) becomes <tt>Just ([PFst, PSnd],
--   x)</tt>.
defaultVarIdents :: [VarIdent]

-- | Given a list of used variable names in the current context, generate a
--   unique fresh name based on a given one.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; print $ refreshVar ["x", "y", "x₁", "z"] "x"
--   x₂
--   </pre>
refreshVar :: [VarIdent] -> VarIdent -> VarIdent

-- | Refresh a name against a <i>set</i> of taken ones.
--   
--   The list version above is O(taken) per call, and naming a whole
--   context calls it once per entry, which made reading the naming off a
--   context with every top-level definition of a project in it quadratic.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; print $ refreshVarIn (Set.fromList ["x", "y", "x₁", "z"]) "x"
--   x₂
--   </pre>
refreshVarIn :: Set VarIdent -> VarIdent -> VarIdent

-- | <a>freshenBinderLeaves</a> against a <i>set</i> of taken names, for
--   the same reason <a>refreshVarIn</a> exists beside <a>refreshVar</a>.
freshenBinderLeavesIn :: Set VarIdent -> Binder -> Binder
incVarIdentIndex :: VarIdent -> VarIdent

-- | Increment the subscript number at the end of the indentifier.
--   
--   <pre>
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; putStrLn $ T.unpack $ incIndex "x"
--   x₁
--   
--   &gt;&gt;&gt; putStrLn $ T.unpack $ incIndex "x₁₉"
--   x₂₀
--   </pre>
incIndex :: Text -> Text
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.Foil.Names.Binder
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.Foil.Names.Proj
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.Foil.Names.TModality
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.Foil.Names.VarIdent
instance GHC.Internal.Data.Foldable.Foldable Language.Rzk.Foil.Names.TypeInfo
instance GHC.Internal.Base.Functor Language.Rzk.Foil.Names.TypeInfo
instance GHC.Internal.Data.String.IsString Language.Rzk.Foil.Names.VarIdent
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Language.Rzk.Foil.Names.VarIdent
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.Foil.Names.TModality
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.Foil.Names.VarIdent
instance GHC.Internal.Data.Traversable.Traversable Language.Rzk.Foil.Names.TypeInfo


-- | The core syntax on <tt>free-foil</tt>.
--   
--   This is the successor of <a>Language.Rzk.Free.Syntax</a>'s
--   <tt>TermF</tt> / <tt>TermT</tt>, built on <a>AST</a> instead of the
--   vendored <tt>Free.Scoped</tt>. It is compiled but not yet consumed:
--   the checker still runs on the old representation, and the two are
--   swapped over in a later stage.
--   
--   Three things carry over unchanged, and are imported rather than
--   duplicated: <a>VarIdent</a> (a surface identifier), <a>Binder</a> (the
--   <i>names</i> a binder introduces, including a pair pattern, which
--   still binds exactly one variable), <a>TModality</a>, and
--   <a>TypeInfo</a> (a node's type plus its memoised weak head and normal
--   forms).
--   
--   What changes is the variable representation. A binder is a
--   <a>NameBinder</a>, a variable is a <a>Name</a> (an <tt>Int</tt>), and
--   weakening a term into a larger scope is <a>sink</a>, a coercion rather
--   than a traversal of every node.
module Language.Rzk.Foil.Syntax

-- | The optional domain annotation of a λ: its modality, its parameter
--   type, and (for a shape) the tope the parameter is restricted by. It
--   was an anonymous triple in the old signature; the generic machinery
--   needs a named type here, and it reads better anyway.
data LambdaParam scope term
LambdaParam :: TModality -> term -> Maybe scope -> LambdaParam scope term
data TermSig scope term
UniverseF :: TermSig scope term
UniverseCubeF :: TermSig scope term
UniverseTopeF :: TermSig scope term
CubeUnitF :: TermSig scope term
CubeUnitStarF :: TermSig scope term
Cube2F :: TermSig scope term
Cube2_0F :: TermSig scope term
Cube2_1F :: TermSig scope term
CubeIF :: TermSig scope term
CubeI_0F :: TermSig scope term
CubeI_1F :: TermSig scope term
CubeProductF :: term -> term -> TermSig scope term
CubeFlipF :: term -> TermSig scope term
CubeUnflipF :: term -> TermSig scope term
CubeSupF :: term -> term -> TermSig scope term
CubeInfF :: term -> term -> TermSig scope term
TopeTopF :: TermSig scope term
TopeBottomF :: TermSig scope term
TopeEQF :: term -> term -> TermSig scope term
TopeLEQF :: term -> term -> TermSig scope term
TopeAndF :: term -> term -> TermSig scope term
TopeOrF :: term -> term -> TermSig scope term
TopeInvF :: term -> TermSig scope term
TopeUninvF :: term -> TermSig scope term
RecBottomF :: TermSig scope term
RecOrF :: [(term, term)] -> TermSig scope term
TypeFunF :: Binder -> TModality -> term -> Maybe scope -> scope -> TermSig scope term
TypeSigmaF :: Binder -> TModality -> term -> scope -> TermSig scope term
TypeIdF :: term -> Maybe term -> term -> TermSig scope term
AppF :: term -> term -> TermSig scope term
LetF :: Binder -> Maybe term -> term -> scope -> TermSig scope term
LambdaF :: Binder -> Maybe (LambdaParam scope term) -> scope -> TermSig scope term
PairF :: term -> term -> TermSig scope term
FirstF :: term -> TermSig scope term
SecondF :: term -> TermSig scope term
ReflF :: Maybe (term, Maybe term) -> TermSig scope term
IdJF :: term -> term -> term -> term -> term -> term -> TermSig scope term

-- | A match over a <tt>#data</tt> scrutinee: scrutinee, optional motive,
--   and one branch per constructor (constructor name, arm chain). The node
--   is elaborated into the generated eliminator during typechecking, so a
--   <i>typed</i> match never exists.
MatchF :: term -> Maybe term -> [(VarIdent, term)] -> TermSig scope term

-- | One branch binder of a match; the body is the next arm, or the branch
--   body once the binders run out. Valid only inside a <a>MatchF</a>
--   branch; the parser cannot produce it anywhere else.
MatchArmF :: Binder -> scope -> TermSig scope term
UnitF :: TermSig scope term
TypeUnitF :: TermSig scope term
TypeAscF :: term -> term -> TermSig scope term
TypeRestrictedF :: term -> [(term, term)] -> TermSig scope term
TypeModalF :: TModality -> term -> TermSig scope term
ModAppF :: TModality -> term -> TermSig scope term
ModExtractF :: TModality -> TModality -> term -> TermSig scope term
LetModF :: Binder -> TModality -> TModality -> Maybe term -> Maybe term -> term -> scope -> TermSig scope term
HoleF :: Maybe VarIdent -> TermSig scope term

-- | Where a term was written.
--   
--   This is the annotation of an <i>untyped</i> term, so that a diagnostic
--   can point at the sub-term it is about rather than at the declaration
--   around it (issue #81). It is a phantom in the node's term parameter:
--   the annotation machinery wants a functor of the term, and a position
--   holds no terms.
newtype SrcPos term
SrcPos :: RzkPosition -> SrcPos term

-- | No position: what a node the checker builds itself carries, and what a
--   node gets until the conversion from the surface syntax puts the real
--   one on it.
noSrcPos :: SrcPos term

-- | An untyped term: the surface syntax, elaborated, every node carrying
--   where it was written.
type Term = AST NameBinder AnnSig SrcPos TermSig

-- | A typed term: every node carries its type. The successor of
--   <tt>TermT</tt>.
type TermT = AST NameBinder AnnSig TypeInfo TermSig

-- | A scope: a binder together with the term it binds over.
type ScopedTermT = ScopedAST NameBinder AnnSig TypeInfo TermSig

-- | A scope of an untyped term.
type ScopedTerm = ScopedAST NameBinder AnnSig SrcPos TermSig

-- | Record where a term was written, unless it is already recorded.
--   
--   The conversion tags a node after converting what is under it, and
--   desugaring hands surface nodes back to the conversion carrying the
--   position of the node they came from. A node that already knows where
--   it was written therefore learnt it from something more specific, and
--   keeps it: the λ that a definition's parameters are wrapped in reuses
--   the λ's own position as it peels them off, and would otherwise claim
--   every diagnostic in the body.
--   
--   A variable carries no node of its own, so it is returned unchanged;
--   where a variable occurrence was written is on its <a>VarIdent</a>
--   instead.
atSrcPos :: forall (n :: S). RzkPosition -> Term n -> Term n

-- | Where the term was written, when it came from a file.
positionOfTerm :: forall (n :: S). Term n -> Maybe RzkPosition

-- | The annotation of a node: its type, and its memoised normal forms. A
--   variable carries none — its type lives in the context.
typeInfoOf :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> Maybe (TypeInfo (TermT n))

-- | Drop every annotation, for printing and for the surface-facing API.
untyped :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> Term n

-- | Memoise a node's own weak head normal form (the self-referential knot
--   of the old representation, unchanged).
termIsWHNF :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> TermT n
termIsNF :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> TermT n

-- | Syntactic equality of two terms of the same scope.
--   
--   Annotation-blind, as the old derived <a>Eq</a> was, but it also
--   requires the two to bind the same names, so it is <i>conservative</i>:
--   two α-equivalent terms whose binders differ are not equal. That is
--   what the tope-context scans want — the terms there come from the same
--   context — and it is cheaper than <a>alphaEqT</a>, which walks the
--   scope.
eqT :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TermT n -> Bool

-- | α-equivalence: name-blind and annotation-blind. The old
--   representation's <a>Eq</a> compared binder names, so <tt>\ x -&gt;
--   x</tt> and <tt>\ y -&gt; y</tt> were unequal; they are the same term,
--   and this says so.
alphaEqT :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> TermT n -> TermT n -> Bool
elemT :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> [TermT n] -> Bool
notElemT :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> [TermT n] -> Bool
nubT :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [TermT n] -> [TermT n]

-- | The free variables of a term.
--   
--   free-foil 0.4.0 exports <tt>freeVarsOf</tt>, but it deduplicates and
--   sorts; this one keeps mention order and repeats, as the old
--   representation's did. A name bound on the way down is dropped from the
--   result, which is what makes the coercion back to the outer scope
--   right.
freeVarsOfTerm :: forall (n :: S). Term n -> [Name n]

-- | The free variables of a typed term, not counting those that occur only
--   in the types of its nodes (<a>Bifoldable</a> skips the annotation, as
--   it did before).
freeVarsOfTermT :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> [Name n]

-- | Does the term mention the universe <tt>U</tt> anywhere? A constructor
--   field whose type does is what makes an inductive type <i>large</i>
--   (see the largeness warning in <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.Decl</a>).
containsUniverse :: forall (n :: S). Term n -> Bool
isHoleT :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> Bool

-- | Is the term a <i>flexible</i> spine: a hole, or an elimination headed
--   by one (<tt>? a b</tt>, <tt>first ?</tt>, <tt>second (? a)</tt>)?
--   
--   Such a term is not yet committed to any shape: filling the head hole
--   can turn it into anything. A type of this form therefore stands for an
--   arbitrary type, which is what lets an eliminator whose result type is
--   a motive application (<tt>ind-path A a C d x p : C x p</tt>) be judged
--   against a concrete goal. Contrast <a>containsHole</a>, which is also
--   true of a term whose <i>shape</i> is already fixed and only has holes
--   among its parts (<tt>? = ?</tt> is an identity type either way).
--   
--   A projection counts for the same reason an application does. <tt>first
--   ?</tt> is whatever the first component of the pair turns out to be, so
--   it has no shape of its own to mismatch with. Without this, a lemma
--   stating a property of projections (<tt>first-path-Σ ... : first s =
--   first t</tt>) is not offered against a goal whose endpoint is a plain
--   variable, because solving <tt>first ?t</tt> against it would mean
--   inventing the pair.
isHoleHeadedT :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> Bool

-- | The name of every hole in a term.
holeNamesOf :: forall (n :: S). Term n -> [Maybe VarIdent]

-- | Does the term contain a hole anywhere (including nested, e.g. <tt>f
--   ?</tt>)?
containsHole :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> Bool

-- | Go under the binder of a scoped term.
--   
--   The binder is used as it stands when its name is free in the ambient
--   scope, which is the common case and costs nothing. It has to be
--   renamed when the name is taken — sinking a term into a scope that has
--   grown since the term was built can do that — and only then is the body
--   traversed.
withScopedT :: forall (sig :: Type -> Type -> Type) (n :: S) r. (Bifunctor sig, Distinct n) => Scope n -> ScopedAST NameBinder sig n -> (forall (l :: S). DExt n l => NameBinder n l -> AST NameBinder sig l -> r) -> r

-- | Go under two scoped terms that stand for <i>one</i> variable.
--   
--   A Π-type and a λ over a shape each carry a tope scope beside the body,
--   under what the user wrote as a single binder. On free-foil each
--   <a>ScopedAST</a> has its own <a>NameBinder</a>, so the second is
--   instantiated with the first's name: they behave as two abstractions
--   over one argument, as they did before.
withScopedT2 :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => Scope n -> ScopedTermT n -> ScopedTermT n -> (forall (l :: S). DExt n l => NameBinder n l -> TermT l -> TermT l -> r) -> r

-- | Open a scoped term with a name that is already in scope.
--   
--   Generic in the signature, so that a λ's (untyped) body and the
--   codomain of the Π it is checked against can be opened under one and
--   the same binder.
openWith :: forall (sig :: Type -> Type -> Type) (n :: S) (l :: S). (Bifunctor sig, DExt n l) => Scope l -> Name l -> ScopedAST NameBinder sig n -> AST NameBinder sig l

-- | Replace a <i>free</i> name by a term.
--   
--   A section's assumption is a free name at the top level, and closing
--   the section abstracts it out of the definitions that use it; this is
--   how those definitions are rewritten. free-foil's substitutions are
--   keyed by a binder, so the map is built directly.
substituteName :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> Name n -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n

-- | Abstract a free name out of a term: the binder the continuation
--   receives binds what the name stood for.
--   
--   The name stays in the scope index (a scope only ever grows), but the
--   term no longer mentions it, which is what makes the resulting Π or λ
--   closed over it.
abstractName :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => Scope n -> Name n -> TermT n -> (forall (l :: S). DExt n l => NameBinder n l -> TermT l -> r) -> r

-- | Instantiate a scoped term with a term: the successor of
--   <tt>substituteT x scope</tt>.
instantiateT :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> ScopedTermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n

-- | Instantiate a scoped <i>untyped</i> term. There are no memoised normal
--   forms to invalidate, so this is free-foil's own substitution.
instantiateUntyped :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> ScopedTerm n -> Term n -> Term n

-- | Substitution that invalidates the memoised normal forms of every node
--   it rebuilds, and substitutes into each node's type.
--   
--   A renaming (<a>substitute</a>) keeps the memo, since a renamed term
--   reduces exactly as the original does. A real substitution does not: a
--   variable is in weak head normal form, and what replaces it need not
--   be. This is one traversal, as substituting and invalidating separately
--   was two.
substituteT :: forall (o :: S) (i :: S). Distinct o => Scope o -> Substitution TermT i o -> TermT i -> TermT o
pattern UniverseT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern UniverseCubeT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern UniverseTopeT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern CubeUnitT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern CubeUnitStarT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern Cube2T :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern Cube2_0T :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern Cube2_1T :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern CubeIT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern CubeI_0T :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern CubeI_1T :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern CubeProductT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern CubeFlipT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern CubeUnflipT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern CubeSupT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n

pattern LambdaT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> Binder -> Maybe (LambdaParam (ScopedAST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n)) -> ScopedAST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern PairT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n

pattern TypeAscT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern TypeRestrictedT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> [(AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n, AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n)] -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern TypeModalT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> TModality -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern ModAppT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> TModality -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern ModExtractT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> TModality -> TModality -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern LetModT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> Binder -> TModality -> TModality -> Maybe (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> Maybe (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> ScopedAST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n
pattern HoleT :: forall {binder} {ann} {n}. ann (AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n) -> Maybe VarIdent -> AST binder (AnnSig ann TermSig) n

-- | The free-foil core back to surface syntax.
--   
--   A transcription of <tt>fromTermWith'</tt> from
--   <a>Language.Rzk.Foil.Names</a>. The structure is the same, and so are
--   the display rules:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>a binder's user-written name is kept, refreshed only against names
--   already in use; an anonymous binder draws from
--   <a>defaultVarIdents</a>;</li>
--   <li>a pattern binder is shown as the pattern, and projections of the
--   variable it binds are folded back to the component names, so a goal
--   reads <tt>\ (t , s) -&gt; …</tt> and not <tt>\ x -&gt; … π₁ x
--   …</tt>;</li>
--   <li>an anonymous binder the codomain does not use is not shown at all,
--   so <tt>(x₁ : A) → B</tt> prints as <tt>A → B</tt>.</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   What changes is the bookkeeping: a variable is a <a>Name</a>, so the
--   display names live in a <a>NameMap</a> keyed by name, rather than
--   being threaded through de Bruijn shifts.
module Language.Rzk.Foil.Print

-- | Print a closed term.
fromTermClosed :: Term 'VoidS -> Term
fromTerm :: forall (n :: S). [VarIdent] -> [VarIdent] -> NameMap n Display -> Term n -> Term

-- | Peel a match branch's arm chain back into its binder patterns and
--   body.
--   
--   Each <a>MatchArm</a> contributes one pattern; the bookkeeping per
--   binder is the same as <a>fromTerm</a> does for a λ (freshen the
--   binder's leaves, record the display name, spend a supply name for a
--   placeholder).
matchArms :: forall (n :: S). [VarIdent] -> [VarIdent] -> NameMap n Display -> Term n -> ([Pattern], Term)

-- | The name standing for the variable itself. A single-variable binder
--   uses its own name; a pattern binder needs a placeholder, which is only
--   shown if the whole point is used (in a shape tope, say), and then it
--   is printed as the pattern anyway.
displayNameOf :: Binder -> [VarIdent] -> VarIdent

-- | Refresh a binder's named leaves against the names already in use; draw
--   fresh names for anonymous leaves from the remaining supply.
freshenBinder :: [VarIdent] -> [VarIdent] -> Binder -> (Binder, [VarIdent])

-- | Does a scope actually use the variable it binds?
--   
--   Compares name <i>ids</i> rather than names, which sidesteps having to
--   unsink the inner scopes' names back into this one. Ids are unique per
--   binder, so a hit is an occurrence of exactly this binder's variable.
--   
--   (free-foil's own <tt>freeVarsOf</tt> would do, but it is not in the
--   0.2.0 release -- it is one of the unreleased helpers on free-foil's
--   <tt>main</tt>.)
scopeUsesItsBinder :: forall (n :: S). ScopedTerm n -> Bool

-- | Every name id occurring in a term, bound or free.
nameIdsOf :: forall (l :: S). Term l -> [Int]


-- | Surface syntax to the free-foil core.
--   
--   A transcription of <tt>toTerm</tt> from
--   <a>Language.Rzk.Foil.Names</a>, with the variable handling replaced.
--   The environment is still a function from a surface identifier to a
--   term, as before; what changes is what happens at a binder:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>a binder is a fresh <a>NameBinder</a> rather than the de Bruijn
--   <tt>Z</tt>;</li>
--   <li>the environment is carried into the binder's scope with
--   <a>sink</a>, which is a coercion, where the old representation shifted
--   every entry with <tt>S &lt;$&gt;</tt> and so rebuilt every term it
--   held.</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   A pattern binder still binds exactly <i>one</i> variable, as before:
--   the components of <tt>\ (t , s) -&gt; …</tt> are projections of it,
--   and <a>Binder</a> records the names so they can be shown back to the
--   user.
module Language.Rzk.Foil.Convert

-- | The environment: what a surface identifier stands for in the current
--   scope. A pattern binder maps its leaves to projections of the single
--   variable it binds, which is why this is a map to <i>terms</i> and not
--   to names.
type Env (n :: S) = VarIdent -> Term n

-- | Translate a closed surface term.
toTermClosed :: Term -> Term 'VoidS

-- | Enter a pattern binder with an explicit continuation for the body:
--   bind one fresh name, map the pattern's leaves to projections of it,
--   and carry the rest of the environment in with <a>sink</a>.
--   <a>toScopedPattern</a> is the plain-body special case; a match branch
--   chains further arms through the continuation.
toScopedPatternWith :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> Pattern -> Env n -> (forall (l :: S). Distinct l => Scope l -> Env l -> Term l) -> ScopedTerm n

-- | Enter a pattern binder over a surface body.
toScopedPattern :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> Pattern -> Env n -> Term -> ScopedTerm n

-- | Enter an anonymous binder (a non-dependent function type binds
--   nothing).
toScopedAnon :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> Env n -> Term -> ScopedTerm n

-- | What each leaf of a pattern stands for: a projection chain over the
--   single variable the pattern binds.
bindings :: forall (n :: S). Pattern -> Term n -> [(VarIdent, Term n)]
toTerm :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> Env n -> Term -> Term n

-- | Elaborate a surface term whose free identifiers are not known in
--   advance.
--   
--   Each identifier occurring anywhere in the term gets a name in a fresh
--   scope, so an <i>open</i> term (the annotation of a binder, say, taken
--   out of its context) can be put into the core, transformed, and printed
--   back with the names it came in with. The reference index needs this:
--   it splits the annotation of a pair binder through the core, and has no
--   typing context to hand.
withOpenTerm :: Term -> (forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> NameMap n Display -> Term n -> r) -> r

-- | Sink an association list of binders by coercion, with no per-entry
--   rebuild (<a>withOpenTerm</a> calls this at every binder it opens).
--   <a>sink1</a> cannot see through the pair (its element must be the sunk
--   type itself), but the sinkability argument is the same: only the names
--   mention the scope, and a name sinks by coercion.
sinkBound :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). DExt n l => [(VarIdent, Name n)] -> [(VarIdent, Name l)]

-- | Every identifier occurring in a piece of surface syntax, bound or
--   free.
collectVarIdents :: Data a => a -> [VarIdent]
nubOrd :: Ord a => [a] -> [a]

module Language.Rzk.VSCode.Config
data ServerConfig
ServerConfig :: Bool -> ServerConfig
[formatEnabled] :: ServerConfig -> Bool
instance Data.Default.Internal.Default Language.Rzk.VSCode.Config.ServerConfig
instance Data.Aeson.Types.FromJSON.FromJSON Language.Rzk.VSCode.Config.ServerConfig
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.VSCode.Config.ServerConfig
instance Data.Aeson.Types.ToJSON.ToJSON Language.Rzk.VSCode.Config.ServerConfig

module Language.Rzk.VSCode.Logging
logDebug :: MonadLsp c m => Text -> m ()
logInfo :: MonadLsp c m => Text -> m ()
logWarning :: MonadLsp c m => Text -> m ()

-- | Error logs will also be shown to the user via `window/showMessage`
logError :: MonadLsp c m => Text -> m ()


-- | Conversion between code-point and UTF-16 positions at the LSP
--   boundary.
--   
--   LSP positions count UTF-16 code units (the default position encoding,
--   and the only one VS Code supports), while alex positions and
--   everything derived from them (the surface AST, the reference index,
--   the typechecker) count Unicode code points. The two agree except on
--   lines containing astral-plane characters (code points above U+FFFF,
--   such as <tt>𝕀</tt>), each of which takes two UTF-16 units. Emitting a
--   code-point column for such a line shifts every position to the right
--   of the character, and a range boundary can land in the middle of a
--   surrogate pair, which is what shatters the glyph in the editor (see
--   issue #303).
--   
--   Everything internal stays in code points; the handlers convert with
--   this module when crossing the wire, in both directions.
--   <a>AstralLines</a> records only the lines where the two encodings
--   differ, so for the common all-BMP document every conversion is an
--   identity after one map lookup.
module Language.Rzk.VSCode.PositionEncoding

-- | The lines of a document on which code-point and UTF-16 columns differ,
--   keyed by 0-based line number.
data AstralLines
astralLines :: Text -> AstralLines

-- | The length of a text in UTF-16 code units.
utf16Length :: Text -> Int

-- | Convert a 0-based code-point column on the given 0-based line to
--   UTF-16 units. A column beyond the end of the line keeps its distance
--   past the end (the diagnostics code uses column 99 to mean "to the end
--   of the line").
colToUtf16 :: AstralLines -> Int -> Int -> Int

-- | Convert a 0-based UTF-16 column on the given 0-based line to code
--   points. A column inside a surrogate pair maps to the start of its
--   character.
colFromUtf16 :: AstralLines -> Int -> Int -> Int

-- | Convert an incoming LSP position (UTF-16) to code points.
positionFromUtf16 :: AstralLines -> Position -> Position

-- | Convert an outgoing range (code points) to UTF-16.
rangeToUtf16 :: AstralLines -> Range -> Range

-- | Convert semantic tokens (code points) to UTF-16. The length is
--   converted through the token's end column, so a token that itself
--   contains astral characters (e.g. the <tt>𝕀</tt> keyword) gets its
--   UTF-16 width.
tokensToUtf16 :: AstralLines -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute] -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]

module Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex
data Uri
Uri :: FilePath -> Uri
[uriPath] :: Uri -> FilePath
data Position
Position :: Int -> Int -> Position
[positionLine] :: Position -> Int
[positionCharacter] :: Position -> Int
data Range
Range :: Position -> Position -> Range
[rangeStart] :: Range -> Position
[rangeEnd] :: Range -> Position
data Location
Location :: Uri -> Range -> Location
[locationUri] :: Location -> Uri
[locationRange] :: Location -> Range
data Binding
Binding :: Text -> Location -> Maybe Text -> [Location] -> Binding
[bindingName] :: Binding -> Text
[bindingDef] :: Binding -> Location

-- | The printed surface annotation of the binder, when it has one (e.g.
--   <tt>A</tt> for <tt>(x : A)</tt>, <tt>I | φ t</tt> for <tt>(t : I | φ
--   t)</tt>). Top-level names carry <a>Nothing</a>; their elaborated type
--   comes from the typecheck cache instead.
[bindingType] :: Binding -> Maybe Text
[bindingRefs] :: Binding -> [Location]
data ReferenceIndex
ReferenceIndex :: Map (FilePath, Int) [(Int, Int, Binding)] -> Map Location AssumeScope -> ReferenceIndex

-- | Every occurrence (definition or reference), keyed by file and line, as
--   column spans; identifiers never span lines. This is what makes
--   <a>lookupAt</a> a map lookup rather than a scan over all bindings.
[occurrences] :: ReferenceIndex -> Map (FilePath, Int) [(Int, Int, Binding)]

-- | The definition sites of <tt>#assume</tt>d names, with their scope.
--   Assumptions do not survive to the typechecked declarations (the
--   section mechanism folds them into the definitions that use them), so
--   the semantic token overlay recognises them here, syntactically. The
--   scope is kept because the two kinds warrant different styling: a
--   top-level assumption is a file-wide axiom (such as function
--   extensionality), while one inside a section is a hypothesis the
--   section abstracts over at its <tt>#end</tt>.
[assumeSites] :: ReferenceIndex -> Map Location AssumeScope
indexModules :: [(FilePath, Module)] -> ReferenceIndex
lookupAt :: ReferenceIndex -> Uri -> Position -> Maybe Binding
bindingSites :: Binding -> [Location]
locationPath :: Location -> FilePath

-- | Every occurrence recorded for a file, with the binding it resolves to:
--   0-based line and column span. Zero-width spans (the derived def
--   entries of generated eliminators) are skipped; they occupy no
--   characters.
fileOccurrences :: ReferenceIndex -> FilePath -> [(Binding, Int, Int, Int)]

-- | Where a name was <tt>#assume</tt>d.
data AssumeScope

-- | outside any section: a file-wide axiom
AssumeTopLevel :: AssumeScope

-- | inside a section: a hypothesis, discharged at <tt>#end</tt>
AssumeInSection :: AssumeScope

-- | The assume-scope of a definition site, if it is one of an
--   <tt>#assume</tt>d name. A local that shadows an assumption resolves to
--   its own binder, not to a site recorded here.
assumeScopeAt :: ReferenceIndex -> Location -> Maybe AssumeScope
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.AssumeScope
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Binding
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Location
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Position
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Range
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Uri
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Location
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Position
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Range
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Uri
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.AssumeScope
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Binding
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Location
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Position
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Range
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.ReferenceIndex
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Language.Rzk.VSCode.ReferenceIndex.Uri

module Language.Rzk.VSCode.Tokenize
tokenizeModule :: Module -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]

-- | Walk the commands tracking the section depth: an assumption outside
--   any section is a file-wide axiom and is marked as an abstract function
--   (see <a>tokenizeCommand</a>), while an assumption inside a section is
--   a hypothesis the section abstracts over at its <tt>#end</tt>, so it
--   keeps the parameter token type and only gains the abstract modifier.
tokenizeCommands :: Int -> [Command] -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeLanguageDecl :: LanguageDecl -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeCommand :: Command -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeDataSort :: DataSort -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeDataBody :: DataBody -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeConstructor :: Constructor -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeDataElim :: DataElim -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeDeclUsedVars :: DeclUsedVars -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeSectionName :: SectionName -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeBind :: Bind -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeParam :: Param -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizePattern :: Pattern -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]

-- | A match branch: the constructor name is an enum member (as constructor
--   uses are), the binders are parameters, the body is an ordinary term.
tokenizeMatchBranch :: MatchBranch -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeTope :: Term -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeTerm :: Term -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeTerm' :: Maybe SemanticTokenTypes -> Term -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeRestriction :: Restriction -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeParamDecl :: ParamDecl -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeModalColon :: ModalColon -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeModality :: Modality -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeModComp :: ModComp -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
tokenizeSigmaParam :: SigmaParam -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]
mkToken :: (HasPosition a, Print a) => a -> SemanticTokenTypes -> [SemanticTokenModifiers] -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]

-- | Highlight the fixed syntax of the language (command names, reserved
--   words, operators) and holes directly from the lexer token stream.
--   
--   This complements <a>tokenizeModule</a>, which highlights identifiers
--   and special term formers from the parsed module. Fixed symbols do not
--   need parsing at all: a <tt>:=</tt> is a <tt>:=</tt> wherever it
--   occurs, and a hole <tt>?</tt> (or <tt>?name</tt>) is its own lexer
--   token. Working on the token stream means that the grammar (and the
--   abstract syntax) does not have to track positions of keywords, and
--   that highlighting keeps working for files that (temporarily) fail to
--   parse.
tokenizeSyntaxSymbols :: Text -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]

-- | How to highlight a lexer token, if at all: fixed symbols by
--   <a>classifySymbol</a>, holes as a distinct token. Identifiers are left
--   to the AST pass (<a>tokenizeModule</a>), which knows their role.
classifyToken :: Tok -> Maybe (Text, SemanticTokenTypes)

-- | How to highlight a fixed symbol of the grammar, if at all.
classifySymbol :: Text -> Maybe SemanticTokenTypes

-- | Combine tokens from the parsed module with tokens from the raw symbol
--   stream. On overlap (same start position) the AST-based token wins,
--   since it carries more precise semantics (e.g. <tt>unit</tt> as an enum
--   member rather than a keyword). The result is sorted by position, as
--   required for the LSP delta encoding.
mergeTokens :: [SemanticTokenAbsolute] -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute] -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]

module Rzk


-- | The formatter is designed in a way that can be consumed both by the
--   CLI and the LSP server.
module Rzk.Format

-- | All indices are 1-based (as received from the lexer) Note: LSP uses
--   0-based indices
data FormattingEdit
FormattingEdit :: Int -> Int -> Int -> Int -> Text -> FormattingEdit
formatTextEdits :: Text -> [FormattingEdit]

-- | Format Rzk code, returning the formatted version. Tabs are normalized
--   to single spaces before formatting.
format :: Text -> Text

-- | Format a whole document, for a consumer that replaces it wholesale
--   (the language server does, so that tab normalization and all
--   formatting rules are applied instead of incremental edits to tabbed
--   source).
--   
--   The document ends in as many newlines as it began with. Formatting is
--   a rewriting of the code, and whether a file ends in a newline is not
--   something it has an opinion on: that is the editor's
--   <tt>insert_final_newline</tt> and whatever else formats the
--   surrounding Markdown. The language server used to send the document
--   with every trailing newline stripped, which silently deleted the final
--   one on each save and left the file failing a <tt>.editorconfig</tt> or
--   Prettier check that no further formatting could satisfy.
formatDocument :: Text -> Text

-- | Format Rzk code from a file
formatFile :: FilePath -> IO Text

-- | Format the file and write the result back to the file.
formatFileWrite :: FilePath -> IO ()

-- | Check if the given Rzk source code is well formatted. This is useful
--   for automation tasks. Tabs are normalized to single spaces before
--   checking.
isWellFormatted :: Text -> Bool

-- | Same as <a>isWellFormatted</a>, but reads the source code from a file.
isWellFormattedFile :: FilePath -> IO Bool

-- | Replace every tab character with a single space. Call this before
--   <a>formatTextEdits</a> so that the lexer and edit positions are
--   consistent (BNFC column counts are undefined when the source contains
--   tabs).
normalizeTabs :: Text -> Text
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.Format.FormattingEdit
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Rzk.Format.FormattingEdit
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.Format.FormattingEdit

module Rzk.Project.Config
data ProjectConfig
ProjectConfig :: [FilePath] -> [FilePath] -> ProjectConfig
[include] :: ProjectConfig -> [FilePath]
[exclude] :: ProjectConfig -> [FilePath]
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.Project.Config.ProjectConfig
instance Data.Aeson.Types.FromJSON.FromJSON Rzk.Project.Config.ProjectConfig
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.Project.Config.ProjectConfig


-- | The geometry behind the SVG rendering of cubes, and nothing else.
--   
--   Rzk renders a (sub)shape of a cube as an SVG diagram: the vertices,
--   edges and faces of the unit cube are projected to the plane through a
--   camera, and each of them is labelled with the term that inhabits it.
--   This module holds the part of that story which knows nothing about
--   terms: the projection matrices, the camera, and <a>renderCube</a>,
--   which draws a cube given only a function saying what (if anything) to
--   draw on each of its parts.
--   
--   Nothing here mentions the type checker, so it is shared by both term
--   representations during the free-foil migration.
module Rzk.Render.Geometry

-- | The name of a vertex of the unit cube, as a string of coordinates
--   (e.g. <tt>"010"</tt>).
type PointId = String

-- | The name of a subshape of the unit cube: its vertices, in order,
--   joined by dashes (e.g. <tt>"000-011"</tt> for an edge, <tt>"000"</tt>
--   for a vertex).
type ShapeId = [PointId]
type Point2D a = (a, a)
type Point3D a = (a, a, a)
type Edge3D a = (Point3D a, Point3D a)
type Face3D a = (Point3D a, Point3D a, Point3D a)
type Volume3D a = (Point3D a, Point3D a, Point3D a, Point3D a)
data CubeCoords2D a b
CubeCoords2D :: [(Point3D a, Point2D b)] -> [(Edge3D a, (Point2D b, Point2D b))] -> [(Face3D a, (Point2D b, Point2D b, Point2D b))] -> [(Volume3D a, (Point2D b, Point2D b, Point2D b, Point2D b))] -> CubeCoords2D a b
[vertices] :: CubeCoords2D a b -> [(Point3D a, Point2D b)]
[edges] :: CubeCoords2D a b -> [(Edge3D a, (Point2D b, Point2D b))]
[faces] :: CubeCoords2D a b -> [(Face3D a, (Point2D b, Point2D b, Point2D b))]
[volumes] :: CubeCoords2D a b -> [(Volume3D a, (Point2D b, Point2D b, Point2D b, Point2D b))]
data Matrix3D a
Matrix3D :: a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> Matrix3D a
data Matrix4D a
Matrix4D :: a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> Matrix4D a
data Vector3D a
Vector3D :: a -> a -> a -> Vector3D a
data Vector4D a
Vector4D :: a -> a -> a -> a -> Vector4D a
rotateX :: Floating a => a -> Matrix3D a
rotateY :: Floating a => a -> Matrix3D a
rotateZ :: Floating a => a -> Matrix3D a
data Camera a
Camera :: Point3D a -> a -> a -> a -> a -> Camera a
[cameraPos] :: Camera a -> Point3D a
[cameraFoV] :: Camera a -> a
[cameraAspectRatio] :: Camera a -> a
[cameraAngleY] :: Camera a -> a
[cameraAngleX] :: Camera a -> a
viewRotateX :: Floating a => Camera a -> Matrix4D a
viewRotateY :: Floating a => Camera a -> Matrix4D a
viewTranslate :: Num a => Camera a -> Matrix4D a
project2D :: Floating a => Camera a -> Matrix4D a
matrixVectorMult4D :: Num a => Matrix4D a -> Vector4D a -> Vector4D a
matrix3Dto4D :: Num a => Matrix3D a -> Matrix4D a
fromAffine :: Fractional a => Vector4D a -> (Point2D a, a)
point3Dto2D :: Floating a => Camera a -> a -> Point3D a -> (Point2D a, a)

-- | What to draw on one part (vertex, edge or face) of a cube.
data RenderObjectData
RenderObjectData :: String -> String -> String -> RenderObjectData
[renderObjectDataLabel] :: RenderObjectData -> String
[renderObjectDataFullLabel] :: RenderObjectData -> String
[renderObjectDataColor] :: RenderObjectData -> String
limitLength :: Int -> String -> String

-- | Apply the term-hiding policy to a cell's render data: drop the
--   <tt>&lt;title&gt;</tt> (the full term) from every cell, and blank the
--   visible label of a proof-coloured (interior) cell. Boundary cells
--   (coloured otherwise) keep their given labels. A no-op when not hiding.
hideTermData :: Bool -> String -> RenderObjectData -> RenderObjectData
renderCube :: (Floating a, Show a) => Camera a -> a -> (String -> Maybe RenderObjectData) -> String
defaultCamera :: Floating a => Camera a


-- | The typing context on free-foil.
--   
--   The successor of <tt>Rzk.TypeCheck</tt>'s <tt>Context var</tt>. Two
--   things change, and they are the point of the migration.
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><i>A variable is a name, and so is a top-level entry.</i> A
--   free-foil term refers to a variable by <a>Name</a> (an <tt>Int</tt>),
--   and by nothing else: there is no way to put a <a>VarIdent</a> inside a
--   term. So a top-level definition is a name too, bound in the outermost
--   scope with no binder above it, and the hypotheses — global and local
--   alike — are one <a>NameMap</a>, looked up in constant time. The old
--   context was an association list keyed by a <tt>var</tt> whose equality
--   walked an <tt>S</tt>-chain; <tt>lookupVarInfo</tt> alone was 11.5% of
--   the checker's time. The surface name of an entry is resolved through
--   <a>ctxNamed</a>.</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   This also gives sections their natural shape. A <tt>#assume</tt>d
--   assumption is an ordinary binder, so the definitions of a section are
--   checked in its scope, and closing the section abstracts the assumption
--   by pairing its binder with the body — no rewrite of the elaborated
--   terms (see <tt>Rzk.TypeCheck.Decl</tt>).
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><i>Entering a binder rebuilds nothing.</i> <a>enterBinder</a>
--   extends the scope and sinks the rest of the context by coercion, so it
--   costs O(1) rather than a walk of the context. The old
--   <tt>enterScopeContext</tt> mapped <tt>S &lt;$&gt;</tt> over the whole
--   context, rebuilding every elaborated term it held; the heap profile
--   showed those forced copies retaining most of the live heap, and
--   <tt>GlobalScopeInfo</tt> / <tt>globalEmbed</tt> (PR #277) exist only
--   to keep that shift off the ~1500 top-level entries. All of that
--   machinery is gone.</li>
--   </ul>
module Rzk.TypeCheck.Context
data Covariance

-- | Positive position.
Covariant :: Covariance

-- | Negative position.
Contravariant :: Covariance

-- | Unknown position.
Invariant :: Covariance
data RenderBackend
RenderSVG :: RenderBackend
RenderLaTeX :: RenderBackend
data Verbosity
Debug :: Verbosity
Normal :: Verbosity
Silent :: Verbosity

-- | Where a diagnostic points.
--   
--   The line and column are the start of whatever the diagnostic is about:
--   the declaration being checked, narrowed to the sub-term as the checker
--   descends into it (see <tt>narrowLocation</tt> in
--   <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.Monad</a>). The surface syntax records the start of a
--   node and not its extent, so there is no end position to carry.
data LocationInfo
LocationInfo :: Maybe FilePath -> Maybe Int -> Maybe Int -> LocationInfo
[locationFilePath] :: LocationInfo -> Maybe FilePath
[locationLine] :: LocationInfo -> Maybe Int
[locationColumn] :: LocationInfo -> Maybe Int

-- | Point a location at a position in the same file.
atPosition :: RzkPosition -> LocationInfo -> LocationInfo

-- | What is known about a hypothesis, local or top-level.
data VarInfo (n :: S)
VarInfo :: TermT n -> Maybe (TermT n) -> TModality -> TModality -> Binder -> Bool -> Bool -> [Name n] -> Maybe LocationInfo -> Maybe (DataRole n) -> Int -> VarInfo (n :: S)
[varType] :: VarInfo (n :: S) -> TermT n
[varValue] :: VarInfo (n :: S) -> Maybe (TermT n)
[varModality] :: VarInfo (n :: S) -> TModality
[varModAccum] :: VarInfo (n :: S) -> TModality

-- | the names the binder introduced, for display only
[varOrig] :: VarInfo (n :: S) -> Binder
[varIsAssumption] :: VarInfo (n :: S) -> Bool
[varIsTopLevel] :: VarInfo (n :: S) -> Bool
[varDeclaredAssumptions] :: VarInfo (n :: S) -> [Name n]
[varLocation] :: VarInfo (n :: S) -> Maybe LocationInfo

-- | the role the entry plays for a <tt>#data</tt> declaration, if any
[varDataRole] :: VarInfo (n :: S) -> Maybe (DataRole n)

-- | the length of the entry's meta-parameter prefix (0 for locals and for
--   declarations with no meta parameters); see
--   <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.MetaPrefix</a>. Recomputed when a section close
--   rewrites the entry's type.
[varMetaPrefix] :: VarInfo (n :: S) -> Int

-- | The role a top-level entry plays for a <tt>#data</tt> declaration. The
--   ι-rule (in <a>Eval</a>) recognises an eliminator head and a
--   constructor-headed scrutinee by these; both entries are otherwise
--   opaque (they carry no value).
--   
--   The argument counts speak of the entry's elaborated type: a
--   constructor takes the datatype's parameters and then its own fields;
--   an eliminator takes the parameters, the motive, one method per
--   constructor (in declaration order), and the scrutinee. Closing a
--   section prepends the section's assumptions uniformly to all entries of
--   a declaration, so <tt>abstractOver</tt> bumps the parameter counts.
data DataRole (n :: S)
DataRole :: Name n -> Int -> DataRoleKind -> DataRole (n :: S)

-- | the type former this entry belongs to
[dataRoleDataType] :: DataRole (n :: S) -> Name n

-- | the datatype parameters the entry takes before anything else
[dataRoleNumParams] :: DataRole (n :: S) -> Int
[dataRoleKind] :: DataRole (n :: S) -> DataRoleKind
data DataRoleKind

-- | a constructor: its sort, its 0-based position among the constructors
--   (= the method index), the number of its own fields after the
--   parameters, and the 0-based positions of its recursive fields (each
--   contributes an induction hypothesis right after the field in the
--   method)
DataConKind :: ConSort -> Int -> Int -> [Int] -> DataRoleKind

-- | an eliminator: the number of methods (one per constructor, in
--   declaration order) and the number of indices of the family; the spine
--   is parameters, motive, methods, indices, scrutinee
DataElimKind :: Int -> Int -> ElimKind -> DataRoleKind

-- | A point constructor inhabits the datatype and the ι-rule dispatches on
--   it as a scrutinee head. A path constructor inhabits an identity type
--   over the datatype, so it can never head a well-typed scrutinee, and
--   the ι-rule must not fire on it: its computation rule is the
--   propositional <tt>compute-</tt> lemma generated alongside the
--   eliminators.
data ConSort
PointCon :: ConSort
PathCon :: ConSort

-- | Which eliminator; the ι-rule is the same for both.
data ElimKind
ElimInd :: ElimKind
ElimRec :: ElimKind

-- | Add one leading parameter (a section assumption made explicit).
bumpDataRoleParams :: forall (n :: S). DataRole n -> DataRole n

-- | A tope, together with the modalities under which it is available.
data ModalTope (n :: S)
ModalTope :: TModality -> TModality -> TermT n -> ModalTope (n :: S)
[tModAccum] :: ModalTope (n :: S) -> TModality
[tModVar] :: ModalTope (n :: S) -> TModality
[tTope] :: ModalTope (n :: S) -> TermT n

-- | The judgement being performed, for tracing and for the error report.
data Action (n :: S)
ActionTypeCheck :: Term n -> TermT n -> Action (n :: S)
ActionUnify :: TermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n -> Action (n :: S)
ActionUnifyTerms :: TermT n -> TermT n -> Action (n :: S)
ActionInfer :: Term n -> Action (n :: S)
ActionContextEntailedBy :: [TermT n] -> TermT n -> Action (n :: S)
ActionContextEntails :: [TermT n] -> TermT n -> Action (n :: S)
ActionContextEntailsUnion :: [TermT n] -> [TermT n] -> Action (n :: S)
ActionWHNF :: TermT n -> Action (n :: S)
ActionNF :: TermT n -> Action (n :: S)
ActionCheckCoherence :: (TermT n, TermT n) -> (TermT n, TermT n) -> Action (n :: S)
ActionCloseSection :: Maybe SectionName -> Action (n :: S)
ActionCheckLetValue :: Maybe VarIdent -> Action (n :: S)

-- | The state of the tope-saturation cache in a <a>Context</a> (see
--   <a>ctxTopesSaturated</a>).
data CachedSaturation (n :: S)

-- | No cache was installed for this tope context (entailment falls back to
--   the per-query pipeline).
SaturationUncached :: CachedSaturation (n :: S)

-- | A deferred pipeline run: forced by the first query under this context.
--   <a>Nothing</a> records that the pipeline errored; queries then fall
--   back, so the error surfaces exactly where it would have.
SaturationCached :: Maybe [[ModalTope n]] -> CachedSaturation (n :: S)
data Context (n :: S)
Context :: Scope n -> NameMap n (VarInfo n) -> Map VarIdent (Name n) -> [Name n] -> [SectionInfo n] -> [ModalTope n] -> [ModalTope n] -> [ModalTope n] -> [[ModalTope n]] -> Maybe Bool -> CachedSaturation n -> Map VarIdent [VarIdent] -> [Action n] -> Int -> Maybe Command -> Maybe LocationInfo -> Verbosity -> Covariance -> Maybe RenderBackend -> Bool -> Bool -> Bool -> [VarIdent] -> Bool -> MetaPrefixSensitivity -> Context (n :: S)

-- | Every name in scope: the top-level entries, the section assumptions
--   and the binders entered on the way here. Substitution and freshness
--   need it.
[ctxScope] :: Context (n :: S) -> Scope n

-- | What each name in scope stands for. Total on <a>ctxScope</a>, which is
--   what <a>lookupName</a> assumes.
[ctxVars] :: Context (n :: S) -> NameMap n (VarInfo n)

-- | The surface name of each top-level entry (and of each named binder),
--   for resolving an identifier the parser produced.
[ctxNamed] :: Context (n :: S) -> Map VarIdent (Name n)

-- | Every name in scope, most recently bound first.
--   
--   The order has to be recorded, not recovered: free-foil refreshes a
--   binder only when its name clashes, so after a substitution an inner
--   binder may well carry a <i>smaller</i> id than an outer one (<tt>\ x2
--   -&gt; \ x1 -&gt; …</tt>), and the ascending order of <a>ctxVars</a> is
--   not the order things were bound in. Display depends on this: names
--   claim their display name oldest-first, so that an inner binder is the
--   one refreshed away from an outer name, and not the other way round.
[ctxBound] :: Context (n :: S) -> [Name n]

-- | The open sections, innermost first. Each records the entries declared
--   in it, so closing it can turn them into declarations.
[ctxSections] :: Context (n :: S) -> [SectionInfo n]

-- | Discreteness axioms for the flat cube variables in scope (a flat point
--   of <tt>2</tt> or <tt>I</tt> is an endpoint). Maintained at binder
--   entry, so entailment does not rescan the context on every query.
[ctxDiscreteTopes] :: Context (n :: S) -> [ModalTope n]
[ctxTopes] :: Context (n :: S) -> [ModalTope n]
[ctxTopesNF] :: Context (n :: S) -> [ModalTope n]
[ctxTopesNFUnion] :: Context (n :: S) -> [[ModalTope n]]
[ctxTopesEntailBottom] :: Context (n :: S) -> Maybe Bool

-- | The saturated alternatives for this tope context, cached at the points
--   where the tope context changes.
[ctxTopesSaturated] :: Context (n :: S) -> CachedSaturation n

-- | The identifiers in scope, keyed by their spelling (a <a>VarIdent</a>
--   compares by spelling and carries the position of its defining
--   occurrence, so the values are what a shadowing report names).
--   
--   The check runs at every binder entry, and scanning every name in scope
--   each time was O(context) per binder — with every top-level definition
--   of a project in scope, that is most of them.
[ctxShadow] :: Context (n :: S) -> Map VarIdent [VarIdent]
[ctxActionStack] :: Context (n :: S) -> [Action n]

-- | The length of <a>ctxActionStack</a>, maintained alongside it:
--   measuring the list on every judgement made each action cost O(depth),
--   and each path O(depth²).
[ctxActionStackDepth] :: Context (n :: S) -> Int
[ctxCurrentCommand] :: Context (n :: S) -> Maybe Command
[ctxLocation] :: Context (n :: S) -> Maybe LocationInfo
[ctxVerbosity] :: Context (n :: S) -> Verbosity
[ctxCovariance] :: Context (n :: S) -> Covariance
[ctxRenderBackend] :: Context (n :: S) -> Maybe RenderBackend

-- | When rendering a diagram, hide the proof term: drop the
--   <tt>&lt;title&gt;</tt> (which carries the full term) from every cell
--   and blank the visible label of proof-coloured (interior) cells,
--   keeping the given boundary labels.
[ctxRenderHideTerm] :: Context (n :: S) -> Bool

-- | When <a>True</a> (the default), an unfilled hole is reported as a
--   <tt>TypeErrorUnsolvedHole</tt>; finished work (and CI) must have no
--   holes. The lenient mode (<a>allowHoles</a>) instead records each
--   hole's goal and context.
[ctxHolesAreErrors] :: Context (n :: S) -> Bool

-- | How holes behave during unification, giving three modes overall. With
--   <a>ctxHolesAreErrors</a> a hole is rejected outright (strict).
--   Otherwise a hole always unifies as a leaf; this flag then chooses what
--   happens when the <i>surrounding</i> structure disagrees: <a>True</a>
--   (the default) defers — any term containing a hole is accepted, for an
--   in-progress sketch — while <a>False</a> keeps such a mismatch an error
--   (<a>structuralHoleUnify</a>).
[ctxDeferHoleMismatches] :: Context (n :: S) -> Bool

-- | Named top-level definitions a hole's candidate list may draw on,
--   beyond the local hypotheses (see <a>withHintLemmas</a>).
[ctxHintLemmas] :: Context (n :: S) -> [VarIdent]

-- | When <a>True</a>, a restriction face or <tt>recOR</tt> guard that
--   overhangs the local tope context (is not entailed by it, while still
--   overlapping it) is reported with a non-fatal hint. Off by default:
--   deciding the overhang costs a solver entailment per face and guard,
--   and the overhang is legitimate (see
--   <tt>happy-restrict-face-not-contained</tt>). Enabled with
--   <tt>#set-option "warn-overhang" "yes"</tt>. The <i>disjointness</i>
--   error next to it is unaffected: a vacuous face is always rejected.
[ctxWarnOverhang] :: Context (n :: S) -> Bool

-- | How sensitively the meta-parameter layer check classifies use
--   positions (see <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.MetaPrefix</a>). Strict by default;
--   set with <tt>#set-option "warn-meta-prefix" = "off" | "structural" |
--   "strict"</tt>.
[ctxMetaPrefixSensitivity] :: Context (n :: S) -> MetaPrefixSensitivity

-- | The sensitivity levels of the meta-parameter layer check.
data MetaPrefixSensitivity

-- | no meta-prefix warnings
MetaPrefixOff :: MetaPrefixSensitivity

-- | warn only at structurally object-level positions
MetaPrefixStructural :: MetaPrefixSensitivity

-- | additionally require an unsaturated schema argument to sit within a
--   top-level receiver's meta prefix (the default)
MetaPrefixStrict :: MetaPrefixSensitivity

-- | An open section: the entries declared in it, newest first.
data SectionInfo (n :: S)
SectionInfo :: Maybe SectionName -> [Name n] -> SectionInfo (n :: S)
[sectionName] :: SectionInfo (n :: S) -> Maybe SectionName
[sectionEntries] :: SectionInfo (n :: S) -> [Name n]
emptyContext :: Context 'VoidS

-- | The tope context of an empty context: <tt>⊤</tt> holds under every
--   modality.
emptyTopeContext :: forall (n :: S). [ModalTope n]

-- | Sink a context along a scope extension. Unsound on its own: leaves
--   <a>ctxScope</a> and <a>ctxVars</a> describing the <i>old</i> scope,
--   and the caller must fix both. See the note above; <a>enterBinder</a>
--   is the only caller.
sinkContextUnchecked :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). DExt n l => Context n -> Context l

-- | Enter the scope of a binder: extend the scope with it, record what it
--   is called and what it stands for, and carry the rest of the context
--   in.
enterBinder :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). DExt n l => NameBinder n l -> VarInfo n -> [ModalTope l] -> Context n -> Context l

-- | Enter a <i>fresh</i> binder: one the checker invents rather than one a
--   term carries (to look under a Π when comparing two of them, say).
withFreshBinder :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => Context n -> VarInfo n -> (forall (l :: S). DExt n l => NameBinder n l -> Context l -> r) -> r

-- | Record the name a binder introduces (if any), for the shadowing check.
addBinderNames :: Binder -> Map VarIdent [VarIdent] -> Map VarIdent [VarIdent]

-- | The identifiers in scope spelled like this one.
shadowedBy :: forall (n :: S). VarIdent -> Context n -> [VarIdent]
sinkVars :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). DExt n l => NameMap n (VarInfo n) -> NameMap n (VarInfo l)
sinkTopes :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). DExt n l => [ModalTope n] -> [ModalTope l]
sinkNamed :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). DExt n l => Map VarIdent (Name n) -> Map VarIdent (Name l)
sinkNames :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). DExt n l => [Name n] -> [Name l]

-- | What a name stands for. Total: every name in scope has an entry.
lookupVarInfo :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> Context n -> VarInfo n

-- | What every name in scope stands for, in no particular order.
varInfos :: forall (n :: S). Context n -> [VarInfo n]

-- | Every hypothesis in scope, oldest binding first (see <a>ctxBound</a>:
--   the ids themselves do not tell us this).
varsInScope :: forall (n :: S). Context n -> [(Name n, VarInfo n)]

-- | The name a surface identifier resolves to, if any.
lookupNamed :: forall (n :: S). VarIdent -> Context n -> Maybe (Name n)

-- | The display binder of a name (the whole pattern, for projection
--   folding).
binderOfName :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> Context n -> Binder
class ModeTheory m
iden :: ModeTheory m => m
comp :: ModeTheory m => m -> m -> m
coe :: ModeTheory m => m -> m -> Bool
isRA :: ModeTheory m => m -> Bool

-- | Accumulate a modality (a lock) over the hypotheses and the topes.
--   
--   Note that top-level entries are <i>not</i> touched: a top-level
--   variable is exempt from the accessibility check (see <tt>infer</tt>),
--   so accumulating a modality over them was work with no observable
--   effect. The old context did it to all ~1500 of them on every modal
--   binder.
applyModality :: forall (n :: S). TModality -> Context n -> Context n

-- | Map the values of a name map, keeping its keys.
mapNameMap :: forall a b (n :: S). (a -> b) -> NameMap n a -> NameMap n b

-- | Replace what a name stands for.
--   
--   Closing a section rewrites the definitions made in it, so that each
--   takes the section's assumptions as explicit parameters; this is how
--   the rewritten entries go back into the context.
insertVarInfo :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> VarInfo n -> Context n -> Context n
isAccessible :: forall (n :: S). ModalTope n -> Bool
filterAccessible :: forall (n :: S). [ModalTope n] -> [ModalTope n]
accessibleTopes :: forall (n :: S). [ModalTope n] -> [TermT n]
plainTope :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> ModalTope n
availableTopes :: forall (n :: S). Context n -> [TermT n]
availableTopesNF :: forall (n :: S). Context n -> [TermT n]

-- | Switch to lenient hole mode: record each hole's goal and context
--   instead of reporting it as an error.
allowHoles :: forall (n :: S). Context n -> Context n

-- | Allow a hole's candidate list to draw on the given named top-level
--   definitions, in addition to the local hypotheses.
withHintLemmas :: forall (n :: S). [VarIdent] -> Context n -> Context n

-- | Within the given action, a hole unifies only as a leaf of an otherwise
--   matching structure: a structural mismatch around a hole stays an error
--   rather than being deferred (see <a>ctxDeferHoleMismatches</a>).
structuralHoleUnify :: forall (n :: S). Context n -> Context n
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Context.ConSort
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Context.ElimKind
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Context.LocationInfo
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Context.MetaPrefixSensitivity
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Context.Verbosity
instance Rzk.TypeCheck.Context.ModeTheory Language.Rzk.Foil.Names.TModality
instance GHC.Classes.Ord Rzk.TypeCheck.Context.Verbosity
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.TypeCheck.Context.LocationInfo
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.TypeCheck.Context.MetaPrefixSensitivity
instance Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.Sinkable Rzk.TypeCheck.Context.ModalTope
instance Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.Sinkable Rzk.TypeCheck.Context.VarInfo


-- | Showing a term to the user.
--   
--   A term of the core names its variables by <a>Name</a> (an
--   <tt>Int</tt>), so anything user-facing — an error, a trace of a
--   judgement, a hole's goal — has to say what each name is <i>called</i>.
--   That is a <a>Naming</a>: a display name and a display binder per name
--   in scope, plus the supply of fresh names for the binders the printer
--   meets on the way down.
--   
--   This replaces the old <tt>var -&gt; VarIdent</tt> threading
--   (<tt>name</tt>, <tt>nameInc</tt>, <tt>BinderNames</tt>,
--   <tt>ppTermInContext</tt> — four copies of the same idea), and with it
--   the unwinding loop that rebuilt those names one binder at a time.
module Rzk.TypeCheck.Display

-- | What every name in scope is called, and what the printer may call the
--   binders it has yet to meet.
data Naming (n :: S)
Naming :: NameMap n Display -> [VarIdent] -> [VarIdent] -> Naming (n :: S)
[namingOf] :: Naming (n :: S) -> NameMap n Display

-- | the display names taken, so a bound binder is refreshed away from them
[namingUsed] :: Naming (n :: S) -> [VarIdent]

-- | the names left over, for anonymous binders
[namingSupply] :: Naming (n :: S) -> [VarIdent]

-- | Read the naming off a context.
--   
--   A named binder keeps its name, refreshed only if an outer name has
--   already taken it. An anonymous one draws from the supply. A pattern
--   binder has its component names freshened as a group, so that the
--   pattern shown in the context and the projections folded inside a term
--   agree on them.
--   
--   Entries are named oldest binding first (see <a>ctxBound</a>), so an
--   outer binder keeps its name and an inner one is the one refreshed away
--   from it.
namingOfContext :: forall (n :: S). Context n -> Naming n

-- | A term already rendered for the user, kept as surface syntax rather
--   than a string so that a consumer may still inspect it.
--   
--   Its <a>Show</a> prints the surface syntax, which is what the old
