--   <tt>Term'</tt> did, so a rendered goal or candidate reads the same as
--   it always has (<tt>\ (t, s) → ?</tt>).
newtype Rendered
Rendered :: Term -> Rendered
[getRendered] :: Rendered -> Term

-- | A term as surface syntax, with the context's names.
--   
--   A binder <i>inside</i> the term is freshened only against the names
--   the term itself mentions — not against everything in scope. A type
--   shows the binder it was written with (<tt>Σ (a : A), B a</tt>), even
--   where the context happens to have an <tt>a</tt> of its own: the two
--   are different variables, and shadowing is what binders are for.
renderTerm :: forall (n :: S). Naming n -> Term n -> Rendered

-- | A term shown to the user.
ppTerm :: forall (n :: S). Naming n -> Term n -> String

-- | A typed term shown as <tt>term : type</tt>, as the old
--   <tt>ppFoldT</tt> did. A variable is shown bare: its type is in the
--   context, not on the node.
ppTermT :: forall (n :: S). Naming n -> TermT n -> String

-- | What a name is called, and the (freshened) binder it was introduced
--   by.
displayOf :: forall (n :: S). Naming n -> Name n -> Display

-- | A variable as the user sees it: a pattern binder shows as its pattern
--   (<tt>(t, s)</tt>), anything else by its display name.
ppName :: forall (n :: S). Naming n -> Name n -> String
panicImpossible :: String -> a
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Display.Rendered
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.TypeCheck.Display.Rendered


-- | The surface-syntax scaffolding of <tt>#data</tt> declarations, kept
--   separate from the monadic checker in <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.Decl</a>.
--   
--   Two things live here, both pure. First, small builders over the
--   surface syntax (<tt>surfaceApps</tt>, <tt>surfacePi</tt>, …) and the
--   preprocessed forms of a declaration (the <a>SortIndex</a> telescope
--   and the <a>DataConSurface</a> constructors). Second, the construction
--   of the generated eliminators: given an <a>ElimSpec</a> — the
--   declaration's data together with the fresh binders of the generated
--   types and the validated endpoint images — <a>elimTerms</a> produces
--   the surface types of <tt>ind-D</tt> and <tt>rec-D</tt> and the path
--   computation rules. The checker then pushes those surface terms through
--   the ordinary elaborator, so nothing here constructs core terms or
--   touches the type-checking monad.
module Rzk.TypeCheck.Decl.Data
addParamDecls :: [ParamDecl] -> Term -> Term

-- | One index of a family, as declared in the sort: its binder (when the
--   sort names it, as in <tt>(n : nat) → U</tt>) and its type.
data SortIndex
SortIndex :: Maybe VarIdent -> Term -> SortIndex
[sortIndexVar] :: SortIndex -> Maybe VarIdent
[sortIndexType] :: SortIndex -> Term

-- | The sort of a constructor: a point constructor returns the declared
--   type; a path constructor returns an identity type over it (spelled
--   <tt>l =_{D …} r</tt>), declaring an identification between the two
--   endpoint terms. Path β-rules are propositional (the generated
--   <tt>compute-</tt> lemmas), following the HoTT-book treatment of higher
--   inductive types.
data DataConSort
DataConPoint :: DataConSort

-- | the endpoints of the declared identification, as written
DataConPath :: Term -> Term -> DataConSort

-- | A constructor, preprocessed at the surface level.
data DataConSurface
DataConSurface :: VarIdent -> [ParamDecl] -> [Term] -> [(Int, [Term])] -> [Term] -> Term -> Term -> [Term] -> [VarIdentToken] -> DataConSort -> DataConSurface
[dataConName] :: DataConSurface -> VarIdent

-- | the field telescope, one entry per bound variable
[dataConFields] :: DataConSurface -> [ParamDecl]

-- | the field patterns as terms, in the same order
[dataConFieldPats] :: DataConSurface -> [Term]

-- | the directly recursive fields (their type is the declared type applied
--   to its parameters and some index terms): 0-based position and the
--   index terms; each contributes an induction hypothesis to the
--   eliminator's method
[dataConRecursive] :: DataConSurface -> [(Int, [Term])]

-- | the index terms of the constructor's return type
[dataConRetIndices] :: DataConSurface -> [Term]

-- | the constructor's full surface type: params → fields → D params
[dataConType] :: DataConSurface -> Term

-- | the non-recursive fields → Unit, for the positivity and largeness
--   checks (a directly recursive field mentions the type legitimately)
[dataConProbe] :: DataConSurface -> Term

-- | the non-recursive field types, for the per-field error message
[dataConNonRec] :: DataConSurface -> [Term]

-- | every binder token of the constructor, for freshening
[dataConLocalNames] :: DataConSurface -> [VarIdentToken]
[dataConSort] :: DataConSurface -> DataConSort
surfacePatternVars :: Pattern -> [VarIdent]
identTokenOf :: VarIdent -> VarIdentToken
surfaceVar :: VarIdent -> Term

-- | A λ over plain (untyped) variable patterns; only ever used in checking
--   position, where the domains come from the expected type.
surfaceLambda :: [VarIdent] -> Term -> Term

-- | The wildcard binder, for a generated λ that ignores an argument.
underscoreIdent :: VarIdent

-- | Every variable-occurrence token in a surface term, collected
--   generically. Used for the endpoint well-formedness check of path
--   constructors, which is deliberately syntactic.
surfaceVarTokens :: Data a => a -> [VarIdentToken]
surfaceApps :: Term -> [Term] -> Term
surfaceAppSpine :: Term -> (Term, [Term])
surfaceArrow :: Term -> Term -> Term

-- | The domains and codomain of a surface Π-chain (domain types only; for
--   the shaped and modal parameter forms the carrier is what matters
--   here).
surfacePiSpine :: Term -> ([Term], Term)

-- | Is the term the given name applied to exactly the given parameter
--   variables (in order, the uniformity requirement) and then exactly
--   <tt>arity</tt> index terms? Returns those index terms. A syntactic
--   check: this is how constructor return types and directly recursive
--   fields are recognised.
dataAppliedIndices :: VarIdent -> [VarIdent] -> Int -> Term -> Maybe [Term]
matchesDataApplied :: VarIdent -> [VarIdent] -> Int -> Term -> Bool
surfacePi :: VarIdent -> Term -> Term -> Term
prefixedIdent :: Text -> VarIdent -> VarIdent

-- | Index into a list that is long enough by construction, panicking with
--   a label instead of the opaque <tt>Prelude.!!</tt> message if that
--   invariant is ever broken. Used where an index is derived from the same
--   data as the list (the induction-hypothesis binders, a constructor's
--   field patterns).
nthByConstruction :: String -> [a] -> Int -> a

-- | The 0-based positions of a constructor's directly recursive fields.
recPositionsOf :: DataConSurface -> [Int]

-- | Everything the pure construction of the eliminators closes over: the
--   declaration's name, its parameters and index telescope, the fresh
--   binders of the generated types (the motive, the scrutinee, the
--   induction hypotheses, the path-method names, and the binders of the
--   inlined transport), the preprocessed constructors, and — for each path
--   constructor — the images of its endpoints under the section being
--   defined. Assembled by <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.Decl</a> once the fresh names
--   are allocated and the endpoints validated.
data ElimSpec
ElimSpec :: VarIdent -> [VarIdent] -> [ParamDecl] -> [VarIdent] -> [ParamDecl] -> VarIdent -> VarIdent -> [VarIdent] -> Maybe [VarIdent] -> VarIdent -> VarIdent -> VarIdent -> [DataConSurface] -> [Maybe ((Term, Term), (Term, Term))] -> ElimSpec
[esName] :: ElimSpec -> VarIdent
[esParamVars] :: ElimSpec -> [VarIdent]
[esParamDecls] :: ElimSpec -> [ParamDecl]
[esIndexVars] :: ElimSpec -> [VarIdent]
[esIndexDecls] :: ElimSpec -> [ParamDecl]
[esMotiveV] :: ElimSpec -> VarIdent
[esScrutV] :: ElimSpec -> VarIdent
[esIhNames] :: ElimSpec -> [VarIdent]
[esMethodVars] :: ElimSpec -> Maybe [VarIdent]
[esEndpointV] :: ElimSpec -> VarIdent
[esPathV] :: ElimSpec -> VarIdent
[esTransportV] :: ElimSpec -> VarIdent
[esConsData] :: ElimSpec -> [DataConSurface]
[esPathData] :: ElimSpec -> [Maybe ((Term, Term), (Term, Term))]

-- | The generated surface types of a declaration's eliminators and the
--   path computation rules, all as surface terms for the ordinary
--   elaborator.
data ElimTerms
ElimTerms :: Term -> Term -> [(VarIdent, Term)] -> ElimTerms

-- | the type of <tt>ind-D</tt> (the dependent eliminator)
[indTypeTerm] :: ElimTerms -> Term

-- | the type of <tt>rec-D</tt> (the non-dependent eliminator)
[recTypeTerm] :: ElimTerms -> Term

-- | one <tt>compute-ind-</tt>/<tt>compute-rec-</tt> lemma per path
--   constructor
[computeRules] :: ElimTerms -> [(VarIdent, Term)]
elimTerms :: ElimSpec -> ElimTerms


-- | Type errors, and how they are shown.
--   
--   An error is captured <i>at its own scope</i>: it packages the context
--   it was raised in, existentially, so its scope index does not escape
--   into the error type. The old representation instead nested the error
--   one <tt>Inc</tt> deeper at every binder (<tt>ScopedTypeError</tt>) and
--   unwound the whole stack at printing time, inventing a name per binder
--   as it went. That unwinding loop, and both of its <tt>FIXME: very
--   inefficient filter</tt> sites, are gone: the context already knows
--   what everything in scope is called (see <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.Display</a>).
--   
--   The error type is therefore <i>not</i> scope-indexed, which is why
--   entering a binder no longer has to re-index the error channel.
module Rzk.TypeCheck.Error
data TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorOther :: String -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorUnify :: TermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorUnifyTerms :: TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorNotPair :: TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorNotModal :: Term n -> TModality -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorModalityMismatch :: TModality -> TModality -> Term n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorUnaccessibleVar :: Name n -> TModality -> TModality -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorNotTypeInModal :: TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorNotFunction :: TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorUnexpectedLambda :: Term n -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorUnexpectedPair :: Term n -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorUnexpectedRefl :: Term n -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorCannotInferBareLambda :: Term n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorCannotInferBareRefl :: Term n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorCannotInferHole :: Term n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorUnsolvedHole :: Maybe VarIdent -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorUndefined :: VarIdent -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorTopeNotSatisfied :: [TermT n] -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorTopeContextDisjoint :: TermT n -> [TermT n] -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorTopesNotEquivalent :: TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorInvalidArgumentType :: Term n -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorDuplicateTopLevel :: [VarIdent] -> VarIdent -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorUnusedVariable :: Name n -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorUnusedUsedVariables :: [Name n] -> Name n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorImplicitAssumption :: (Name n, TermT n) -> Name n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorNotIntervalCube :: String -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorRepeatedBinder :: VarIdent -> [VarIdent] -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorMatchScrutineeNotData :: TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorMatchCannotInfer :: Term n -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorMatchMissingBranch :: VarIdent -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorMatchDuplicateBranch :: VarIdent -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorMatchUnknownBranch :: VarIdent -> [VarIdent] -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorMatchBranchArity :: VarIdent -> Int -> Int -> TypeError (n :: S)
TypeErrorReascribedTypeMismatch :: VarIdent -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeError (n :: S)

-- | An error, together with the context it was raised in.
--   
--   The scope index is existential: an error raised under a binder is
--   <i>already</i> complete (its context says what its names are called),
--   so it needs nothing from the enclosing scope and can be thrown
--   straight through it.
data TypeErrorInScopedContext
[TypeErrorInScopedContext] :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Context n -> TypeError n -> TypeErrorInScopedContext
ppModality :: TModality -> String
data OutputDirection
TopDown :: OutputDirection
BottomUp :: OutputDirection
block :: OutputDirection -> [String] -> String
namedBlock :: OutputDirection -> String -> [String] -> String
ppTypeError :: forall (n :: S). Naming n -> TypeError n -> String
ppAction :: forall (n :: S). Naming n -> Int -> Action n -> String

-- | The context an error was raised in: where it happened, what was being
--   checked, the tope context, the stack of judgements, and the
--   hypotheses.
ppContext :: forall (n :: S). OutputDirection -> Context n -> String

-- | An error, with the context it was raised in.
ppTypeErrorInScopedContext :: OutputDirection -> TypeErrorInScopedContext -> String
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Error.OutputDirection


-- | The checker's monad.
--   
--   <tt>TypeCheck n</tt> is the old <tt>TypeCheck var</tt> with the scope
--   index in place of the variable type. The error channel, though, is
--   <i>not</i> indexed: an error carries the context it was raised in (see
--   <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.Error</a>). That is what makes <a>inContext</a> a
--   one-liner — running a judgement in an inner scope is just running it
--   under a different reader, with nothing to re-index on the way out. The
--   old <tt>closeScope</tt> had to wrap the error one binder deeper and
--   re-emit the holes.
module Rzk.TypeCheck.Monad

-- | A binding shown in a hole's local context: the display name and its
--   type, already rendered.
data HoleEntry
HoleEntry :: VarIdent -> Rendered -> HoleEntry
[holeEntryName] :: HoleEntry -> VarIdent
[holeEntryType] :: HoleEntry -> Rendered

-- | The structured goal and context at a hole, recorded in lenient mode
--   (see <a>allowHoles</a>). Everything is rendered to user-facing names
--   at record time, so <a>HoleInfo</a> is independent of the scope it came
--   from. Local hypotheses are split into ordinary term variables and cube
--   variables (the cube/tope layer is specific to Rzk); the global
--   environment is deliberately excluded — it belongs in a searchable
--   inventory, not the goal panel.
data HoleInfo
HoleInfo :: Maybe VarIdent -> Rendered -> Maybe (VarIdent, Rendered) -> [HoleEntry] -> [HoleEntry] -> [Rendered] -> [Rendered] -> [Rendered] -> Maybe String -> Maybe LocationInfo -> HoleInfo

-- | the <tt>?name</tt>, if the hole was named
[holeName] :: HoleInfo -> Maybe VarIdent

-- | expected type (the goal), kept symbolic
[holeGoal] :: HoleInfo -> Rendered

-- | when the goal is a <i>shape</i> (the hole is the argument of a
--   shape-restricted function), the shape's bound variable and its tope:
--   the goal then reads <tt>(binder : holeGoal | tope)</tt>.
--   <a>Nothing</a> for an ordinary goal. (Extension-type goals need no
--   special handling — they are already a restricted type in
--   <a>holeGoal</a>.)
[holeGoalShape] :: HoleInfo -> Maybe (VarIdent, Rendered)

-- | local hypotheses whose type is not a cube
[holeTermVars] :: HoleInfo -> [HoleEntry]

-- | local cube variables (type is a cube)
[holeCubeVars] :: HoleInfo -> [HoleEntry]

-- | local tope assumptions (excluding ⊤)
[holeTopes] :: HoleInfo -> [Rendered]

-- | elimination spines over the local hypotheses whose type fits the goal,
--   with applied arguments left as holes. Already rendered, like the rest.
[holeCandidates] :: HoleInfo -> [Rendered]

-- | introduction forms for the goal type, built from its head constructor
--   with the constituents left as holes. Already rendered, like the rest.
[holeIntroductions] :: HoleInfo -> [Rendered]

-- | an SVG of the goal cell, when the goal is a renderable shape (an
--   arrow, triangle, or square up to dimension 3).
[holeDiagram] :: HoleInfo -> Maybe String
[holeLocation] :: HoleInfo -> Maybe LocationInfo

-- | A non-fatal finding of the checker, recorded on the writer channel
--   beside the holes and carried out of a run in <tt>Checked</tt>.
--   Structured, so the CLI, the LSP, and (later) safe mode each decide how
--   to present or escalate it.
data CheckWarning
LargeInductiveTypeWarning :: VarIdent -> VarIdent -> Maybe LocationInfo -> CheckWarning
MetaPrefixWarning :: VarIdent -> VarIdent -> Int -> Int -> MetaPrefixRule -> Maybe LocationInfo -> CheckWarning

-- | Where a warning points, for per-file attribution.
warningLocation :: CheckWarning -> Maybe LocationInfo

-- | Which candidate rule of the meta-parameter layer check flags a
--   <a>MetaPrefixWarning</a> (see <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.MetaPrefix</a>): the
--   structural rule, or only its stricter variant. Both are emitted so the
--   two candidate defaults can be measured on a corpus side by side.
data MetaPrefixRule
MetaPrefixBoth :: MetaPrefixRule
MetaPrefixStrictOnly :: MetaPrefixRule

-- | What a run records besides its result: the holes it found and the
--   non-fatal findings it made. Both accumulate in reverse and are turned
--   around by <a>checkLog</a> when the run ends.
data CheckLog
CheckLog :: [HoleInfo] -> [CheckWarning] -> CheckLog
[logHolesRev] :: CheckLog -> [HoleInfo]
[logWarningsRev] :: CheckLog -> [CheckWarning]
emptyCheckLog :: CheckLog

-- | What a run recorded, in the order it was recorded.
checkLog :: CheckLog -> ([HoleInfo], [CheckWarning])

-- | The record of a run is kept in the <i>state</i>, beneath the error
--   channel, rather than on a writer channel above it.
--   
--   The two differ exactly where a caught error is concerned: a writer
--   discards what the failing action wrote, and the state keeps it. That
--   is what the checker wants. A command that fails still reports the
--   holes the user wrote in it, and checking goes on to the next command
--   with those holes in hand (see <tt>withCommand</tt> in
--   <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.Decl</a>). A probe that wants the older behaviour
--   asks for it, with <a>suppressing</a>.
type TypeCheck (n :: S) = ReaderT Context n ExceptT TypeErrorInScopedContext State CheckLog

-- | Run a judgement in a given context, keeping what it recorded.
runTypeCheckWith :: forall (n :: S) a. Context n -> TypeCheck n a -> (Either TypeErrorInScopedContext a, ([HoleInfo], [CheckWarning]))

-- | Run a judgement in the empty context, discarding the holes it records.
runTypeCheck :: TypeCheck 'VoidS a -> Either TypeErrorInScopedContext a

-- | Run a judgement in a given context, discarding the holes it records.
runTypeCheckIn :: forall (n :: S) a. Context n -> TypeCheck n a -> Either TypeErrorInScopedContext a

-- | Run a judgement in another scope's context.
--   
--   The error channel and the hole channel are shared and carry no scope
--   index, so there is nothing to translate: this is <a>runReaderT</a>
--   with the inner scope's context, lifted back. Holes recorded inside
--   land in the same state, and an error thrown inside already carries its
--   own context.
inContext :: forall (l :: S) a (n :: S). Context l -> TypeCheck l a -> TypeCheck n a

-- | Raise a type error, capturing the context it happened in.
issueTypeError :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => TypeError n -> TypeCheck n a
issueWarning :: forall (n :: S). String -> TypeCheck n ()
trace' :: Verbosity -> Verbosity -> String -> a -> a
traceTypeCheck :: forall (n :: S) a. Verbosity -> String -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a
localVerbosity :: forall (n :: S) a. Verbosity -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a
localRenderBackend :: forall (n :: S) a. Maybe RenderBackend -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a
localHideTerm :: forall (n :: S) a. Bool -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a
localWarnOverhang :: forall (n :: S) a. Bool -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a
localMetaPrefixSensitivity :: forall (n :: S) a. MetaPrefixSensitivity -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a

-- | Render the enclosed action with the proof term hidden.
hidingTerm :: forall (n :: S) a. TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a
switchVariance :: forall (n :: S) a. TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a
setVariance :: forall (n :: S) a. Covariance -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a

-- | The depth of nested judgements at which type checking gives up.
--   Well-typed input stays far below it; the cap catches a non-terminating
--   search. FIXME: expose as a parameter (<tt>--max-depth</tt> and
--   <tt>rzk.yaml</tt>).
maxActionStackDepth :: Int
performing :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => Action n -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a

-- | Point the location at the sub-term an action is about.
--   
--   The checker descends through <a>performing</a>, so the location
--   narrows as it goes and an error is reported where the sub-term that
--   caused it was written, rather than at the declaration it is in (issue
--   #81). A judgement about a term the checker built itself carries no
--   position, and leaves the location as it found it: that is the
--   innermost enclosing term the user did write.
narrowLocation :: forall (n :: S). Action n -> Maybe LocationInfo -> Maybe LocationInfo
modifyLog :: forall (n :: S). (CheckLog -> CheckLog) -> TypeCheck n ()

-- | Run a probe for its answer alone, discarding whatever it records.
--   
--   A hole's inventory is built by trying candidate moves and seeing which
--   fit, and each trial checks terms of its own; their holes and warnings
--   are not the user's and must not reach the report. This is what the
--   writer channel's <tt>censor</tt> did before the record moved into the
--   state: the state survives an error, so it is put back on that path
--   too.
suppressing :: forall (n :: S) a. TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a
recordHoleInfo :: forall (n :: S). HoleInfo -> TypeCheck n ()
recordCheckWarning :: forall (n :: S). CheckWarning -> TypeCheck n ()
withLocation :: forall (n :: S) a. LocationInfo -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Monad.CheckWarning
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Monad.HoleEntry
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Monad.HoleInfo
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Monad.MetaPrefixRule
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.TypeCheck.Monad.CheckWarning
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.TypeCheck.Monad.HoleEntry
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.TypeCheck.Monad.HoleInfo
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.TypeCheck.Monad.MetaPrefixRule


-- | Entering a scope, evaluation, and the tope solver.
--   
--   These three are one recursive knot and cannot be separated:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>entering a binder needs <a>whnfT</a>, to see whether a flat
--   variable is a point of a cube and so brings a discreteness axiom with
--   it;</li>
--   <li><a>whnfT</a> strips an extension type's restrictions, which asks
--   the solver whether a face's tope holds (<a>checkTope</a>);</li>
--   <li><a>nfT</a> normalises under a binder and under a tope
--   (<a>localTope</a>);</li>
--   <li>and the solver normalises the topes it reasons about
--   (<a>nfTope</a>).</li>
--   </ul>
module Rzk.TypeCheck.Eval

-- | Look up a name and project one field of its <a>VarInfo</a>.
infoOfVar :: forall (n :: S) a. (VarInfo n -> a) -> Name n -> TypeCheck n a
valueOfVar :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> TypeCheck n (Maybe (TermT n))
typeOfVar :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)
modalityOfVar :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> TypeCheck n TModality
locksOfVar :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> TypeCheck n TModality
isTopLevelVar :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> TypeCheck n Bool

-- | Is a surface name defined?
checkDefinedVar :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => VarIdent -> TypeCheck n ()
typeOfUncomputed :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)
typeOf :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | The free variables of a typed term, including those that occur only in
--   the <i>types</i> of the variables it mentions.
--   
--   A definition can depend on a section assumption without naming it:
--   through the type of something else it uses. Closing a section has to
--   see that dependency, and it is exactly what distinguishes an implicit
--   assumption from an explicit one.
freeVarsDeep :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> TypeCheck n [Name n]
nubNames :: forall (n :: S). [Name n] -> [Name n]
elemName :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> [Name n] -> Bool
notElemName :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> [Name n] -> Bool

-- | Instantiate a scoped term with an argument: the old
--   <tt>substituteT</tt>.
instantiate :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => ScopedTermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | The discreteness axiom a flat cube variable brings with it: a flat
--   point of <tt>2</tt> (or of <tt>I</tt>) is one of the endpoints.
--   Maintained at binder entry so that entailment does not have to rescan
--   the context on every query.
discreteAxiomOf :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). (Distinct n, DExt n l) => TModality -> TermT n -> Maybe (TermT n) -> NameBinder n l -> TypeCheck n [ModalTope l]

-- | What a binder adds to the context.
binderInfo :: forall (n :: S). Binder -> TModality -> TermT n -> Maybe (TermT n) -> Maybe LocationInfo -> VarInfo n

-- | Run an action under a binder that has already been chosen.
underBinder :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S) a. (Distinct n, DExt n l) => NameBinder n l -> Binder -> TModality -> TermT n -> Maybe (TermT n) -> TypeCheck l a -> TypeCheck n a

-- | Enter a fresh binder (one the checker invents) and run an action whose
--   result says nothing about the new scope.
withBinder :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => Binder -> TModality -> TermT n -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => NameBinder n l -> TypeCheck l a) -> TypeCheck n a
withFreshIn :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => Scope n -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => NameBinder n l -> r) -> r

-- | Open a scoped term under its own binder, run the action on the body,
--   and pack the result back up as a scoped term.
underScope :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Binder -> TModality -> TermT n -> Maybe (TermT n) -> ScopedTermT n -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => TermT l -> TypeCheck l (TermT l)) -> TypeCheck n (ScopedTermT n)

-- | Like <a>underScope</a>, for a Π (or a λ over a shape), which binds a
--   tope scope beside the body under what the user wrote as one binder.
underScope2 :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Binder -> TModality -> TermT n -> ScopedTermT n -> ScopedTermT n -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => TermT l -> TermT l -> TypeCheck l (TermT l, TermT l)) -> TypeCheck n (ScopedTermT n, ScopedTermT n)

-- | Open a scoped term for a computation whose result says nothing about
--   the new scope (a check, or a rendered string).
inScope :: forall (sig :: Type -> Type -> Type) (n :: S) a. (Bifunctor sig, Distinct n) => Binder -> TModality -> TermT n -> ScopedAST NameBinder sig n -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => AST NameBinder sig l -> TypeCheck l a) -> TypeCheck n a

-- | Like <a>inScope</a>, for a binder that stands for a known value (a
--   <tt>let</tt>).
inScopeWith :: forall (sig :: Type -> Type -> Type) (n :: S) a. (Bifunctor sig, Distinct n) => Binder -> TModality -> TermT n -> Maybe (TermT n) -> ScopedAST NameBinder sig n -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => AST NameBinder sig l -> TypeCheck l a) -> TypeCheck n a

-- | Open a scoped term with a binder that has just been entered.
--   
--   The scoped term lives in the enclosing scope, and so may be the
--   codomain of the type a λ is being checked against, or the tope of a
--   shape: all of them are opened under the <i>one</i> binder the λ
--   introduces.
openScoped :: forall (sig :: Type -> Type -> Type) (n :: S) (l :: S). (Bifunctor sig, DExt n l) => NameBinder n l -> ScopedAST NameBinder sig n -> TypeCheck l (AST NameBinder sig l)

-- | A scope that does not use its binder: the codomain of a non-dependent
--   function type, say.
constScope :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (ScopedTermT n)

-- | Enter the binder of an <i>untyped</i> scope — the body of a λ, or of a
--   let, as the user wrote it — and elaborate it into a typed one.
--   
--   The binder comes from the term being checked, and the scopes of the
--   <i>type</i> it is checked against are opened under that same binder
--   with <a>openScoped</a>.
elaborateUnder :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Binder -> TModality -> TermT n -> Maybe (TermT n) -> ScopedTerm n -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => NameBinder n l -> Term l -> TypeCheck l (TermT l)) -> TypeCheck n (ScopedTermT n)

-- | Enter the binder of an untyped scope and run a computation under it.
--   
--   The result may not mention the new scope — but a <a>ScopedAST</a>
--   <i>hides</i> its scope, so the continuation can pack whatever it built
--   with the binder it was given and hand back as many scoped terms as it
--   likes. That is how a λ returns its elaborated body, its shape tope and
--   the type it turned out to have, all at once.
checkUnderWith :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => Binder -> TModality -> TermT n -> Maybe (TermT n) -> ScopedTerm n -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => NameBinder n l -> Term l -> TypeCheck l a) -> TypeCheck n a
checkUnder :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => Binder -> TModality -> TermT n -> ScopedTerm n -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => NameBinder n l -> Term l -> TypeCheck l a) -> TypeCheck n a
enterModality :: forall (n :: S) b. Distinct n => TModality -> TypeCheck n b -> TypeCheck n b

-- | Assume a tope for the enclosed action.
localTope :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a

-- | Install a deferred saturation cache for the transformed context, and
--   run the action with it.
--   
--   The pipeline's effects are discharged purely into a thunk: installing
--   costs nothing, holes recorded by the speculative run are discarded,
--   and a pipeline error (a tope guard with a hole in lenient mode, say,
--   which the per-query path would never have evaluated) becomes
--   <a>Nothing</a>, so errors surface exactly where they did before.
withRefreshedTopes :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => (Context n -> Context n) -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a

-- | Run a check in every alternative of a disjunctive tope context.
inAllSubContexts :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TypeCheck n () -> TypeCheck n () -> TypeCheck n ()
eqModalTope :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => ModalTope n -> ModalTope n -> Bool
nubModalTopes :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [ModalTope n] -> [ModalTope n]
elemModalTope :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => ModalTope n -> [ModalTope n] -> Bool

-- | Monadic <a>all</a> that stops at the first failing element.
allM :: Monad m => (a -> m Bool) -> [a] -> m Bool
entailM :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [ModalTope n] -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool

-- | The preprocessing <a>entailM</a> does before searching: dedup, split
--   off the context's disjunctions, and saturate each alternative. Depends
--   only on the given topes (plus the discreteness axioms of the context),
--   not on the goal.
saturateForEntailment :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [ModalTope n] -> TypeCheck n [[ModalTope n]]

-- | Search each saturated alternative for the goal.
entailSaturatedM :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [[ModalTope n]] -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool

-- | Entailment against the context's own tope context, using the cached
--   saturation when one was installed. Matching on the payload of
--   <a>SaturationCached</a> is what forces the deferred pipeline, so the
--   cost is paid at the first query under a context, and never for one
--   that is never queried.
entailContextM :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool
saturateTopes :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [ModalTope n] -> [ModalTope n]
saturateInv :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [ModalTope n] -> TypeCheck n [ModalTope n]

-- | Ex falso for BOT, lifted across modalities.
--   
--   A contradiction in the topes that are genuinely available at the
--   identity modality entails BOT, and BOT entails <tt>_μ BOT</tt> for
--   every modality <tt>μ</tt> by the absurd rule (this holds for BOT
--   specifically; a general tope <tt>φ</tt> does NOT give <tt>_μ φ</tt>,
--   which would need the missing unit <tt>id ⇒ μ</tt>). Re-asserting
--   <tt>_μ BOT</tt> at each lock <tt>μ</tt> where an available tope was
--   hidden lets the contradiction survive the lock: <tt>_b BOT</tt> is
--   accessible under a <tt>_b</tt> lock (<tt>coe Flat Flat</tt>), so
--   <tt>mod _b recBOT</tt> in a vacuous context is accepted.
--   
--   A tope counts as available at the identity modality when its variable
--   modality coerces into <tt>Id</tt>: a <tt>_b</tt>-modal tope qualifies
--   via the counit (<tt>coe Flat Id</tt>), but a <tt>_#</tt>-modal one
--   does not (<tt>coe Sharp Id</tt> is False) — which is exactly why
--   <tt>_# BOT</tt> does not leak to plain BOT.
saturateBottom :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [ModalTope n] -> [ModalTope n]
saturateWith :: (a -> [a] -> Bool) -> ([a] -> [a] -> [a]) -> [a] -> [a]
generateTopes :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [TermT n] -> [TermT n] -> [TermT n]

-- | Is this cube point a lattice term (a <tt>sup</tt> or <tt>inf</tt>)?
--   Used to keep the lattice-specific solver work (equality-to-order
--   generation, the antisymmetry fallback for equality goals) off the
--   equality-heavy non-lattice fragment, where it would only cost time
--   without proving anything new.
isLatticePoint :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> Bool
generateTopesForPointsM :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [TermT n] -> TypeCheck n [TermT n]
allTopePoints :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> [TermT n]
topePoints :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> [TermT n]
subPoints :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> [TermT n]

-- | Simplify the context, including disjunctions.
simplifyLHSwithDisjunctions :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [ModalTope n] -> [[ModalTope n]]
solveRHSM :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [ModalTope n] -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool
solveRHS :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [TermT n] -> TermT n -> Bool

-- | Accumulate a modality over a list of topes.
applyModalityToTopes :: forall (n :: S). TModality -> [ModalTope n] -> [ModalTope n]
partitionAccessible :: forall (n :: S). [ModalTope n] -> ([ModalTope n], [ModalTope n])
checkTope :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool
checkTopeEntails :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool
checkEntails :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool
contextEntails :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n ()

-- | Is the local tope context contradictory (does it entail ⊥)?
contextEntailsBottom :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TypeCheck n Bool
topesEquiv :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool

-- | Check that the local tope context is included in (entails) the union
--   of the given topes. This is the COVERAGE obligation of <tt>recOR</tt>:
--   every point of the context must be covered by some branch guard.
--   
--   Only coverage is required, not equivalence: branch guards may overhang
--   the context (when splitting with an already-defined shape, say), so we
--   do not require <tt>OR(guards) |- context</tt>.
contextEntailsUnion :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [TermT n] -> TypeCheck n ()

-- | Diagnose a <tt>recOR</tt> branch guard or a restriction face against
--   the local tope context. There are three cases, by how the tope relates
--   to the context:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>DISJOINT — the tope and a consistent context have empty overlap
--   (their conjunction is ⊥). The face or branch is then vacuous
--   everywhere, so this is a hard error.</li>
--   <li>OVERHANG — the tope is not entailed by the context but still
--   overlaps it. This is allowed and often intentional (splitting or
--   restricting with an already-defined shape, whose faces live on the
--   whole cube rather than being relativised to the context), so we only
--   emit a non-fatal hint.</li>
--   <li>CONTAINED — the tope entails the context: nothing to report.</li>
--   </ul>
checkTopeAgainstContext :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => String -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n ()
stripTypeRestrictions :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> TermT n

-- | The term a restriction face pins down, when one of the faces holds.
tryRestriction :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (Maybe (TermT n))

-- | Perform at most one η-expansion at the top level, to assist
--   unification.
etaMatch :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Maybe (TermT n) -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n, TermT n)
etaExpand :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)
inCubeLayer :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool
inTopeLayer :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool

-- | Memoise a term's WHNF on its top node without reducing the term
--   itself.
--   
--   The returned term has the same (unreduced) structure, so free-variable
--   and <tt>uses</tt> detection see exactly what the user wrote, while a
--   later <a>whnfT</a> is O(1) via the cached form. Used when storing a
--   definition's elaborated type and value, where an in-place reduction
--   could otherwise discard or expose a variable occurrence.
memoizeWHNF :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)
whnfT :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | The branch of a <tt>recOR</tt> (or the face of a restriction) whose
--   guard holds.
firstMatching :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [(TermT n, TermT n)] -> TypeCheck n (Maybe (TermT n))

-- | The head of an application spine and its arguments, in application
--   order, each paired with the type annotation of its <a>AppT</a> node
--   (needed to rebuild a neutral application).
collectAppSpine :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> (TermT n, [(TypeInfo (TermT n), TermT n)])

-- | Apply a function term to a spine of arguments, reducing.
applySpine :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> TermT n -> [(TypeInfo (TermT n), TermT n)] -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | Try to fire a <tt>#data</tt> ι-rule on an application spine: the head
--   is a generated eliminator, the scrutinee argument is headed by a fully
--   applied constructor of the same datatype. Returns the method applied
--   to the constructor's fields (and any leftover spine arguments),
--   unreduced.
--   
--   A non-<a>Var</a> head answers <a>Nothing</a> immediately, so the
--   common neutral spine pays one pattern match; a <a>Var</a> head pays
--   one <a>lookupVarInfo</a>.
tryDataElimStep :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> [(TypeInfo (TermT n), TermT n)] -> TypeCheck n (Maybe (TermT n))

-- | Apply a term to arguments left to right, annotating each application
--   node with its actual type. The spine machinery reuses the annotations
--   of existing nodes, which a freshly built ι-redex does not have.
applyTyped :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> [TermT n] -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | Peel the head's syntactic lambda chain into one substitution, then
--   reduce. <tt>subst</tt> maps the binders consumed so far to their
--   arguments; <tt>body</tt> is the current lambda's body, at the scope
--   those binders extended into.
peelLambdas :: forall (i :: S) (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> Substitution TermT i n -> TermT i -> [(TypeInfo (TermT n), TermT n)] -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | Apply a non-lambda (already WHNF) function to a spine, one argument at
--   a time: this is the type-directed part of application, unchanged from
--   before.
applyNeutral :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> TermT n -> [(TypeInfo (TermT n), TermT n)] -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | Apply a non-lambda function <tt>f'</tt> (already WHNF) to one argument
--   <tt>x</tt>. A shape-restricted function contributes a tope
--   side-condition; a function whose return type is restricted refines the
--   application's type; everything else is a neutral application.
--   Extracted verbatim from the old single-argument <tt>AppT</tt> case.
applyWhnfFun :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TypeInfo (TermT n) -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)
nfSupT :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n
nfInfT :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n
nfTope :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)
nfT :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)


-- | The meta-parameter layer check.
--   
--   The type theory implemented in rzk separates a /meta-theoretic
--   parameter layer/ from the object theory (RSTT proper): see §3.2 of the
--   Rzk paper (Kudasov, Sim, Ahrens, "Rzk: a Proof Assistant for Synthetic
--   ∞-Categories", <a>arXiv:2607.12207</a>), where a statement is
--   abstracted over a context of schematic cube, tope, and type
--   parameters. The checker did not enforce responsible use of this layer.
--   Per declaration, the <i>meta prefix</i> is the parameter prefix up to
--   and including the last parameter whose type lives outside RSTT proper:
--   a universe, <tt>CUBE</tt>, <tt>TOPE</tt>, or a Π-type quantifying over
--   or landing in one of those. Interleaved object parameters are swept
--   in, which only strengthens the check.
--   
--   The discipline: the meta prefix must be fully supplied wherever the
--   declaration is used at an object-level position; unsaturated use at a
--   meta-typed position is legitimate macro-level plumbing and stays
--   allowed. Then the development reads as a family of object-theory
--   definitions, one per meta instantiation.
--   
--   Positions are classified structurally, on the elaborated term:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>the root of a declaration's type and value is meta (a definition
--   may alias a schema), and a λ-body inherits its λ's position (the
--   value's leading λs are the declaration's own parameters);</li>
--   <li>an application argument is meta when the function's Π-domain at
--   that position is meta-shaped (the receiver declared a schema
--   parameter);</li>
--   <li>the components of type formers are meta (types are the schema
--   layer), except the endpoints of an identity type, which are
--   terms;</li>
--   <li>everything else (pair components, projections, <tt>recOR</tt>
--   branches, a <tt>let</tt>-bound value, …) is an object position.</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   The strict rule (the default, see <a>MetaPrefixSensitivity</a>)
--   additionally requires an unsaturated schema argument to sit within a
--   <i>top-level</i> receiver's meta prefix. This also polices meta-shaped
--   domains that only arise by instantiating a receiver's object
--   parameters with large types (as in composing schema-level implications
--   with a generic <tt>comp</tt>); such uses are emitted with the distinct
--   code <a>MetaPrefixStrictOnly</a>, so the structural sensitivity can
--   silence them without losing the rest.
--   
--   Known blind spot: under type-in-type, an impredicative instantiation
--   can forge a meta-shaped argument domain out of an object parameter —
--   with <tt>g : (X : U) → X → X</tt>, in <tt>g ((X : U) → X → X)
--   my-id</tt> the second domain is meta-shaped only because <tt>X</tt>
--   was instantiated with a large type. The structural sensitivity reads
--   such a position as meta and stays silent. The strict default flags it
--   when the argument falls outside the receiver's meta prefix (as here),
--   but a forgery landing <i>within</i> the prefix, or behind a λ-bound
--   receiver, still passes: deciding whether an instantiation is genuinely
--   impredicative is level inference, a separate (planned) analysis, not
--   this check.
module Rzk.TypeCheck.MetaPrefix

-- | The length of the meta prefix of a declaration with this type: the
--   number of leading parameters up to and including the last meta one (0
--   when there is none). Never throws.
metaPrefixOf :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n Int

-- | Does this type live outside RSTT proper — is it a universe,
--   <tt>CUBE</tt>, <tt>TOPE</tt>, or a Π-type that quantifies over or
--   lands in one of those? This covers a family into a universe (<tt>A →
--   U</tt>, a tope family) and a schematic type such as <tt>(X : U) → X →
--   X</tt> (predicatively both are large). A parameter of such a type is a
--   meta parameter. Never throws; an unanswerable probe reads as object.
isMetaType :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool

-- | Walk a declaration's elaborated type and value, warning about every
--   use of a top-level name that supplies fewer arguments than its meta
--   prefix at an object-level position. Advisory: never throws, and runs
--   silently so WHNF probes do not trace.
recordMetaPrefixUses :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => VarIdent -> TermT n -> Maybe (TermT n) -> TypeCheck n ()
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.MetaPrefix.PosKind


-- | Normalisation by evaluation, used as an all-or-nothing fast path for
--   conversion checking.
--   
--   <a>nbeConvertible</a> evaluates both sides into a value domain with
--   closures (sharing by construction: a definition's value is evaluated
--   once per occurrence, not once per copy, and Haskell's laziness makes
--   the evaluation call-by-need) and compares the values structurally,
--   with one-step η for lambdas and pairs mirroring <a>etaMatch</a>.
--   Evaluation is emph{glued}: a spine over a definition keeps the spine
--   as well as its unfolding, and the unfolding is lazy. Two spines over
--   the same definition are then compared argument by argument, without
--   unfolding it. Only where the spines disagree is an unfolding forced.
--   
--   It answers only <a>Convertible</a> or <a>DontKnow</a>, never a
--   definite inequality, so a caller falls back to the ordinary
--   unification on <a>DontKnow</a>. The two cases are not opposites, which
--   is why the answer is not a <a>Bool</a>. The fast path can therefore
--   accept more than the unification below it, but never less. Note that
--   it does accept more. The ordinary path decomposes an application
--   pairwise, which invents subgoals that a βδ-equal but structurally
--   different pair need not meet (see <a>unifyViaDecompose</a>).
--   
--   Soundness is a subset argument: <a>Convertible</a> is answered only
--   for terms that are βδ-convertible up to α and the one-step η above,
--   with every construct whose <i>reduction</i> consults the context —
--   <tt>recOR</tt> guard selection, holes, the modal constructs —
--   evaluating to an opaque <a>VAbort</a> that poisons the comparison into
--   <a>DontKnow</a>. Extension types and <tt>recBOT</tt> are compared
--   structurally (see the note at their <a>eval</a> case): a structurally
--   identical pair of restricted types is also accepted by the ordinary
--   unification, through reflexive coverage and the cross-face coherences
--   already proved at formation. Every <a>Convertible</a> is therefore
--   also a success of the old unification.
--   
--   The evaluator is a pure function of the <a>Context</a>:
--   <tt>valueOfVar</tt> is a plain reader-only lookup, and fresh variables
--   for comparing closures are de Bruijn levels (<a>HFresh</a>), so the
--   foil scope machinery is never extended and no quote function is
--   needed.
--   
--   <h2>Attribution</h2>
--   
--   None of the underlying techniques are ours. Semantic conversion
--   checking — evaluate both sides into a value domain with closures and
--   compare the values, applying functions to fresh generic values — is
--   the algorithm of Coquand, <i>An algorithm for type-checking dependent
--   types</i> (Science of Computer Programming 26, 1996), the
--   implementation-level core of normalisation by evaluation (Berger and
--   Schwichtenberg, LICS 1991).
--   
--   Comparing two stuck terms by their spines, head first and arguments
--   pairwise, rather than by normalising them, is the algorithmic equality
--   of Abel and Coquand, /Untyped Algorithmic Equality for Martin-Löf's
--   Logical Framework with Surjective Pairs/ (Fundamenta Informaticae
--   77(4):345–395, 2007; TLCA 2005), see
--   <a>https://www2.tcs.ifi.lmu.de/~abel/lfsigma.pdf</a>.
--   
--   The representation we use for it is the emph{glued evaluation} of
--   András Kovács' <a>smalltt</a>. Its README states the tension as "in
--   basic conversion checking, we want to evaluate as efficiently as
--   possible; in quoting, we want to output terms which are as small as
--   possible". It resolves the tension by evaluating a top-level variable
--   to "values which represent lazy ('non-deterministic') choice between
--   unfolding the definition, and not unfolding it". Following smalltt,
--   <a>conv</a> also speculates: "whenever we have the same top-level head
--   symbol on both sides, we try to unify the spines", and unfolds only
--   when that fails. smalltt separates its modes and uses gluing for
--   quoting small terms as well. This module has no quote function, so it
--   needs neither. The general implementation shape, environment machines
--   with closures and de Bruijn levels for fresh variables, follows the
--   same author's <a>elaboration-zoo</a>.
--   
--   For the fragment this module deliberately aborts on (tope-indexed
--   reduction such as <tt>recOR</tt>), the template is cubical: Sterling
--   and Angiuli, <i>Normalization for Cubical Type Theory</i> (LICS 2021),
--   and its implementation lineage in <tt>cooltt</tt>.
--   
--   What is specific to rzk is only the packaging: the all-or-nothing
--   gating (<a>Convertible</a> or <a>DontKnow</a>, never refute), and
--   <a>VAbort</a> poisoning of the context-sensitive fragment so that the
--   fast path stays sound by a subset argument.
module Rzk.TypeCheck.NbE

-- | The answer of the fast path.
--   
--   Note that the two cases are not opposites, so this is deliberately not
--   a <a>Bool</a>: <a>DontKnow</a> is never a refutation, and a caller may
--   not read it as one.
data Conversion

-- | Definitely convertible, by the module's soundness argument.
Convertible :: Conversion

-- | No answer. The two terms may well be convertible, and the caller falls
--   back to the ordinary unification to find out.
DontKnow :: Conversion

-- | Are the two terms definitely convertible?
nbeConvertible :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n Conversion
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.NbE.Conversion
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.NbE.DeBruijnLevel
instance Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.InjectName Rzk.TypeCheck.NbE.Val
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.TypeCheck.NbE.Conversion


-- | Drawing a term as an SVG diagram of a cube.
--   
--   The geometry lives in <a>Rzk.Render.Geometry</a>; what is here is the
--   part that knows about terms: which subshape of the cube a tope carves
--   out, which term inhabits each of them, and what to label it with.
module Rzk.TypeCheck.Render
cube2powerT :: forall (n :: S). Int -> TermT n
splits :: [a] -> [([a], [a])]
verticesFrom :: forall (n :: S). [TermT n] -> [(ShapeId, TermT n)]
subTopes2 :: forall (n :: S). Int -> TermT n -> [(ShapeId, TermT n)]
componentWiseEQT :: forall (n :: S). Int -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n

-- | Is the variable an anonymous one (written <tt>_</tt>)? Its cells are
--   left unlabelled.
isAnonymous :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> TypeCheck n Bool

-- | Render a term in the current context.
ppInContext :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> TypeCheck n String
renderObjectsFor :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => String -> Int -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n [(ShapeId, RenderObjectData)]
renderObjectsInSubShapeFor :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => String -> Int -> [Name n] -> Name n -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n [(ShapeId, RenderObjectData)]
renderForSubShapeSVG :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => String -> Int -> [Name n] -> Name n -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n String
renderForSVG :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => String -> Int -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n String
drawCube :: Int -> [(String, RenderObjectData)] -> String

-- | The dimension of a cube, if it is a power of the directed interval.
dimOf :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> Maybe Int
maxRenderDim :: Int
renderTermSVGFor :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => String -> Int -> (Maybe (TermT n, TermT n), [Name n]) -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n (Maybe String)

-- | Enter a binder and assume the shape tope it carries, if any.
inScopeMaybeTope :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => Binder -> TModality -> TermT n -> Maybe (ScopedTermT n) -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => NameBinder n l -> TypeCheck l a) -> TypeCheck n a
renderTermSVG :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (Maybe String)

-- | Render the goal <i>cell</i> for a (shape) type: introduce an abstract
--   inhabitant and render it with the proof term hidden. Under a boundary
--   tope an abstract inhabitant of an extension type reduces to the
--   prescribed face value, so the cell shows its given edges with a blank
--   interior — the shape to inhabit, not an answer. <a>Nothing</a> for a
--   non-shape type (a 0-cell, or a non-cube goal).
renderGoalCellSVG :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (Maybe String)
renderTermSVG' :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (Maybe String)

-- | Render a term of a function type by applying it to the variable it
--   abstracts over, and drawing that.
renderApplied :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). DExt n l => NameBinder n l -> TermT n -> TermT n -> ScopedTermT n -> TypeCheck l (Maybe String)


-- | Unification, which in rzk is really subtyping: an extension type's
--   faces, a shape's tope and the variance of the position all take part.
module Rzk.TypeCheck.Unify

-- | Open two scoped terms under <i>one</i> binder, so that the two sides
--   of a comparison are compared as functions of the same variable.
inScope2 :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => Binder -> TModality -> TermT n -> ScopedTermT n -> ScopedTermT n -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => NameBinder n l -> TermT l -> TermT l -> TypeCheck l a) -> TypeCheck n a

-- | α-equivalence in the ambient scope.
alphaEq :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool

-- | Run <tt>check super sub</tt> on the pair <tt>(expected, actual)</tt>,
--   oriented by the ambient variance. Under <a>Covariant</a> the expected
--   type is the supertype and under <a>Contravariant</a> the actual one
--   is. <a>Invariant</a> is normally handled upstream by running both
--   directions; we run both here as well, for safety.
bySubtyping :: forall (n :: S). (TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n ()) -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n ()

-- | The domain of a shape-indexed function is contravariant, so the
--   subtype's domain tope has to hold wherever the supertype's does.
--   Shared by Π-types and by the lambdas that inhabit them.
domainEntails :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n ()
unifyTopes :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n ()
unify :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Maybe (TermT n) -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n ()

-- | The syntactic fast path.
--   
--   α-equivalence, not the structural equality the old representation
--   used: two terms that differ only in a binder's name are the same term,
--   and saying so here saves the whole unification below.
unifyViaDecompose :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n ()
unifyTypes :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n ()
unifyTerms :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n ()
checkCoherence :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => (TermT n, TermT n) -> (TermT n, TermT n) -> TypeCheck n ()
unifyInCurrentContext :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Maybe (TermT n) -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n ()


-- | The judgements — <tt>typecheck</tt> and <tt>infer</tt> — and the hole
--   inventory.
--   
--   The two belong together: checking a hole records its goal and context,
--   and recording a hole probes what could fill it, which typechecks and
--   unifies candidate terms.
module Rzk.TypeCheck.Judgements
isCubeType :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> Bool

-- | Is a (WHNF) goal type in the cube or tope layer, so that a hole of
--   this type is a cube point or a tope rather than a term? Used to
--   suppress the type-layer-specific hole candidates (<tt>recOR</tt>,
--   <tt>recBOT</tt>), which cannot inhabit a cube or a tope.
isCubeOrTopeType :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> Bool

-- | The names in scope a new one would shadow.
doesShadowName :: forall (n :: S). VarIdent -> TypeCheck n [VarIdent]
checkTopLevelDuplicate :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => VarIdent -> TypeCheck n ()
checkNameShadowing :: forall (n :: S). VarIdent -> TypeCheck n ()

-- | A fresh hole of the given type.
mkHole :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> TermT n

-- | A hole carrying a name, so a suggested move can say what each of its
--   holes stands for: <tt>id-hom ?A ?x</tt> rather than <tt>id-hom ?
--   ?</tt>. The name is the Π binder's, so the move reads like the lemma's
--   own signature, and two spines of the same lemma applied to different
--   numbers of arguments are told apart by what the extra holes are
--   called.
mkNamedHole :: forall (n :: S). Maybe VarIdent -> TermT n -> TermT n

-- | The constructors of a <tt>#data</tt> type former, in declaration
--   order; empty for anything else. Found by their roles: the type former
--   itself carries none, so the scan is over the names in scope.
dataConstructorsOf :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> TypeCheck n [Name n]

-- | The generated eliminators of a <tt>#data</tt> type former
--   (<tt>ind-D</tt> before <tt>rec-D</tt>), with their roles.
dataEliminatorsOf :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> TypeCheck n [(Name n, DataRole n)]

-- | A term of the given type built as λ-binders over a single typed hole
--   (structurally: the motive types the generator builds are literal
--   Π-chains). The eliminators pass such a motive so that their result
--   type β-reduces to the hole and fits any goal, exactly like
--   <tt>idJ</tt>'s motive.
lambdaHoleOf :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Set VarIdent -> Scope n -> TermT n -> TermT n

-- | A match over a hypothesis, one branch per constructor with a hole
--   body: the notational candidate offered beside the
--   <tt>ind-</tt>/<tt>rec-</tt> spines. The node is display-only (its
--   annotations are dropped before rendering), so its type infos are
--   holes. Branch binders reuse the constructor's declared field names,
--   with an induction hypothesis named <tt>ih</tt>, freshened against the
--   names taken at the hole exactly as <a>lambdaHoleOf</a> freshens its
--   motive binders.
matchHoleOf :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Context n -> Set VarIdent -> Scope n -> Int -> [Name n] -> TermT n -> TermT n

-- | Apply a term along its Π-type: a <a>Just</a> is the argument to use, a
--   <a>Nothing</a> becomes a typed hole. Stops when the plan runs out.
applyPlan :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> [Maybe (TermT n)] -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | How many <i>branching</i> eliminators <a>allEliminationsInto</a> will
--   chain.
--   
--   A forced Π-application is free (see <a>allEliminationsInto</a>), so
--   this bounds only the Σ/cube projections and <tt>idJ</tt> steps, not
--   the argument count of a spine. A temporary fixed bound: branching is
--   shallow in the goals seen so far (a few projections), and a larger
--   bound mostly adds self-referential spines (a built result eliminated
--   again).
maxEliminationDepth :: Int

-- | Whether eliminating a value spends the search budget. A forced
--   Π-application is a <a>SpineStep</a> — there is one way to fill the
--   argument (with a hole), so <a>allEliminationsInto</a> applies it for
--   free; a <a>Branching</a> eliminator (a Σ/cube projection or
--   <tt>idJ</tt>) costs one against <a>maxEliminationDepth</a>.
data ElimCost
SpineStep :: ElimCost
Branching :: ElimCost

-- | All ways to eliminate a hypothesis into a value usable at a goal.
--   
--   Given a <tt>target</tt> type and a hypothesis <i>term</i>, return
--   every elimination spine over that term whose type fits the target (or
--   a subtype of it). Arguments introduced by application are left as
--   holes for the caller to fill later. A value that already fits is
--   returned as-is; a function is applied to holes; a Σ-type (or anything
--   that unfolds to one, e.g. <tt>is-contr</tt>) is projected, possibly
--   repeatedly — so <tt>first (first (is-segal-A ? ? ? ? ?))</tt> is
--   discovered.
--   
--   A Π-application is a forced spine step, so it extends the spine for
--   free and does not spend the budget. Only the genuinely branching
--   eliminators count against <a>maxEliminationDepth</a>, so the bound
--   limits real search depth, not argument count, and a lemma that must be
--   applied to many holes is still reached.
--   
--   A spine over a top-level hypothesis is emitted only once its meta
--   prefix (see <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.MetaPrefix</a>) is fully applied: an
--   unsaturated schema is not a suggestion, mirroring the warn-meta-prefix
--   discipline. The search still passes through the unsaturated stages, so
--   the saturated spines behind them are found; only the emission is
--   gated.
allEliminationsInto :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> Set VarIdent -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n [TermT n]

-- | Whether a term of the given (whnf) type may stand where a value of the
--   <tt>target</tt> type is expected: the two types unify under
--   <a>structuralHoleUnify</a>, so a hole acts as a wildcard leaf but a
--   structural mismatch around it is still a mismatch (an under-applied
--   function does not match an extension-type goal, but a partial
--   application that genuinely fits an ordinary-function goal does).
--   
--   The exception is a <i>flexible</i> type, one headed by a hole: it has
--   no shape to mismatch with, so it fits any target. This is what makes
--   an eliminator stated over a motive usable as a candidate ---
--   <tt>ind-path ? ? ? ? ? ?</tt> has type <tt>?C ?x ?p</tt> and so is
--   offered at every goal, exactly as <tt>idJ</tt> already is, with the
--   motive and the base case left as holes.
--   
--   Outer type restrictions are stripped from both sides first: an
--   extension-type boundary is satisfied by later refinement, not by the
--   choice of spine, and matching against the restricted goal would reject
--   the very spine that introduces the holes meant to satisfy it (<tt>f
--   ?</tt> at a boundary goal, say).
--   
--   Holes or constraints recorded while probing are discarded, so this is
--   a pure yes/no query.
fitsInto :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool

-- | The eliminators a value of the given (weak head normal) type admits,
--   each as a function wrapping the eliminated term, paired with its
--   <a>ElimCost</a>.
--   
--   A Π-type is eliminated by application to a fresh hole (a spine step);
--   a Σ-type by either projection; an identity type by path induction
--   (<tt>idJ</tt>), with the motive and base case left as holes. The
--   projections and <tt>idJ</tt> branch. Anything else admits no simple
--   eliminator.
--   
--   The names taken at the hole (the source namespace) are passed in so
--   that every binder an eliminator introduces (the <tt>idJ</tt> motive's
--   <tt>\ b q → ?</tt>, a data eliminator's motive λs) is named in the
--   move, freshened against them.
eliminatorsOf :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Set VarIdent -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n [(ElimCost, TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n))]

-- | A scoped term that does not use its binder.
closedScope :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> (forall (l :: S). () => TermT l) -> ScopedTermT n

-- | The motive <tt>\ b q → ?</tt> of a path induction: a type in the two
--   motive binders, left as a hole.
motiveOf :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Set VarIdent -> Scope n -> TermT n -> TermT n -> TermT n

-- | The binder for a λ introduced over a domain type.
--   
--   A binder the type already gives as a pattern is kept as-is — it
--   carries the user's own names (<tt>(t , s)</tt>). Otherwise an
--   <i>explicit</i> (pre-whnf) Σ-type or product domain is destructured
--   into a fresh pair pattern, recursively for products, so that a
--   nameless <tt>2 × 2 × 2</tt> parameter is introduced as <tt>((t1 , t2)
--   , t3)</tt> rather than a single opaque variable. Any other domain
--   keeps its single binder.
--   
--   Leaves are named by what they range over: a cube-product component is
--   a point, named <tt>tN</tt>; a Σ component is a term, named
--   <tt>xN</tt>. The names are display-only (the body is a hole that does
--   not mention them) and carry a shared running index, so every leaf in
--   the pattern is distinct.
destructuringBinder :: forall (n :: S). Binder -> TermT n -> Binder

-- | All ways to introduce a value <i>of</i> a goal type by its head
--   constructor, leaving the constituents as holes:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>a Π-type is introduced by a λ-abstraction over a hole body (<tt>\
--   x -&gt; ?</tt>); the binder is taken from the type, so a pattern
--   domain (a <tt>Δ²</tt> point <tt>(t , s)</tt>, say) is introduced as
--   <tt>\ (t , s) -&gt; ?</tt>;</li>
--   <li>a Σ-type or a cube product by a pair of holes (<tt>(? ,
--   ?)</tt>);</li>
--   <li>an identity type by <tt>refl</tt>, but only when its two endpoints
--   already agree (otherwise <tt>refl</tt> would not typecheck);</li>
--   <li>the unit type by <tt>unit</tt>;</li>
--   <li>the tope universe by each tope constructor — <tt>TOP</tt>,
--   <tt>BOT</tt>, <tt>? ≡ ?</tt>, <tt>? ≤ ?</tt>, <tt>? ∧ ?</tt>, <tt>? ∨
--   ?</tt> — so a shape (a hole of type <tt>TOPE</tt>) can be built up by
--   tapping.</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   Unlike <a>allEliminationsInto</a> this does not search: a type has at
--   most one introduction form (the tope universe is the one exception),
--   read off its head constructor. Outer restrictions are stripped first,
--   so an extension type is introduced by the form of its underlying type
--   (its boundary is met by later refinement of the holes, not by the
--   choice of constructor).
--   
--   The λ binder of a Π-introduction is freshened against the names
--   already visible at the hole, so introducing over a type whose own
--   definition reuses an in-scope name (<tt>hom</tt>, whose internal
--   binder is <tt>t</tt>) yields <tt>\ t₁ -&gt; ?</tt> rather than a
--   <tt>t</tt> that shadows the existing one.
allIntroductionsOf :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> Set VarIdent -> TypeCheck n [TermT n]

-- | Apply a term to holes through its whole Π-telescope: a datatype former
--   applied through its parameters, so a <tt>U</tt>-goal offers <tt>coprod
--   ? ?</tt>.
saturateWithHoles :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | Whether the two endpoints of an identity type are definitionally
--   equal, so that <tt>refl</tt> inhabits it. Like <a>fitsInto</a>, any
--   holes or constraints recorded while probing are discarded, leaving a
--   pure yes/no query.
endpointsAgree :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n Bool

-- | Ex falso: in a contradictory tope context <tt>recBOT</tt> inhabits any
--   type, so it is a candidate for every goal there (and only there —
--   elsewhere it would not typecheck). Independent of the goal and of the
--   local hypotheses.
recBottomCandidates :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TypeCheck n [TermT n]

-- | Whether the local tope context is covered by the union of the given
--   topes — the coverage obligation of <tt>recOR</tt>, as a yes/no query
--   rather than a check that issues an error.
coverageHolds :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [TermT n] -> TypeCheck n Bool

-- | Tope case-split moves: ways to build a value of the goal by
--   <tt>recOR</tt>, splitting the proof over a cover of the local tope
--   context. Three sources, offered together (the UI ranks and filters):
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li>each disjunction <tt>ψ ∨ φ</tt> already in the context becomes
--   <tt>recOR(ψ ↦ ?, φ ↦ ?)</tt> — its cover is immediate;</li>
--   <li>when the goal is an extension type, its restriction faces are a
--   cover candidate, offered only when they actually cover the context (so
--   the move typechecks);</li>
--   <li>a generic two-way split <tt>recOR(? ↦ ?, ? ↦ ?)</tt> with the
--   guards left as holes, for an unusual split the player fills in by
--   hand.</li>
--   </ul>
--   
--   All three are offered only where a split makes sense — a cube variable
--   is in scope, the context has a non-trivial tope, or the goal is a
--   restricted type — so an ordinary (tope-free) goal is left alone.
recOrCandidates :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n [TermT n]

-- | The local hypotheses: everything in scope that is not a top-level
--   entry.
localHypotheses :: forall (n :: S). Context n -> [(Name n, VarInfo n)]

-- | The allow-listed top-level lemmas a hole's candidate list may draw on.
lemmaHypotheses :: forall (n :: S). Context n -> [(Name n, VarInfo n)]

-- | The elaboration environment at the current position: every in-scope
--   entry contributes its source name — a pattern its leaves, as
--   projection chains over the variable it binds — and an inner binding
--   wins, exactly as the elaborator resolves an identifier written here.
--   Kept as a table so <a>sourceResolvesTo</a> and <a>parsesBackTo</a>
--   share it.
positionTable :: forall (n :: S). Context n -> Map VarIdent (Term n)

-- | Does this variable's own source name, written at the current position,
--   resolve back to it?
sourceResolvesTo :: forall (n :: S). Map VarIdent (Term n) -> VarIdent -> Name n -> Bool

-- | Does a rendered move, inserted as source text at the current position,
--   parse and resolve back to the very term it renders? The comparison is
--   α-equivalence of the untyped skeletons: a move is well-typed by
--   construction, and insertion is a question of naming. This is the exact
--   form of the old referability guard, and it enforces the move contract
--   for everything emitted — a shadowing or unresolvable name anywhere in
--   the rendering shows up as a resolution difference and drops the move.
parsesBackTo :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Map VarIdent (Term n) -> TermT n -> Rendered -> TypeCheck n Bool

-- | Collapse a literal pair of matching projections, recursively along the
--   pair spine: <tt>(π₁ p, π₂ p)</tt> reads back as <tt>p</tt>. This is
--   exactly what the whole-point rendering of a pattern-bound variable
--   parses to (the pattern <tt>(x, y)</tt> resolves to the projections),
--   so the comparison in <a>parsesBackTo</a> absorbs the
--   projection-folding convention.
pairEtaCollapse :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> Term n -> Term n

-- | Collapse a variable bound by the unit pattern to the constructor. A
--   <tt>\ unit → …</tt> binds a point of <tt>Unit</tt> whose whole-point
--   rendering (and the only way to write it) is <tt>unit</tt>, which
--   parses back as the constructor. The two are the same point of the
--   singleton, so the comparison in <a>parsesBackTo</a> treats them as
--   one, exactly as <a>pairEtaCollapse</a> absorbs the projection-folding
--   convention.
unitPointCollapse :: forall (l :: S). IntSet -> Term l -> Term l

-- | Record the goal and local context at a hole (lenient mode only).
recordHole :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Maybe VarIdent -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n ()

-- | Record a hole. When the hole is the argument of a shape-restricted
--   function its goal is a <i>shape</i>: the cube <tt>goalTy</tt> together
--   with a membership tope, which is a scope over the shape's bound
--   variable. It is rendered under that binder, so the goal reads
--   <tt>(binder : goalTy | tope)</tt>.
recordHoleShape :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Maybe VarIdent -> TermT n -> Maybe (Binder, ScopedTermT n) -> TypeCheck n ()

-- | Check a hole that appears as the argument of a shape-restricted
--   function, whose domain is the cube <tt>cube</tt> restricted by
--   <tt>tope</tt> (a scope over the domain's bound variable). Mirrors the
--   hole case of <a>typecheck</a>, but records the shape as the hole's
--   goal so the diagnostic shows <tt>(binder : cube | tope)</tt>.
checkHoleAgainstShape :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Maybe VarIdent -> Binder -> TermT n -> ScopedTermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | Check a <tt>recOR</tt> against a known expected type: each branch is
--   checked against it under its own guard, the branches must agree on
--   their overlaps, and together they must cover the context.
checkRecOrAgainst :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> [(Term n, Term n)] -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | Drop the restriction faces of an extension type that are vacuous in
--   the current tope context (their overlap with the context is the empty
--   tope ⊥). A face mentioning an unfilled hole cannot be decided, so it
--   is kept. Non-extension types are returned unchanged. Used when
--   descending into a recOR branch, where the sibling branches' faces are
--   disjoint from the branch guard.
pruneVacuousFaces :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)
typecheck :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Term n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | How a match elaborates: which eliminator it targets, and — for
--   <tt>ind-D</tt> — which variable scrutinee (if any) to abstract out of
--   the goal when building the motive. Computed once from the
--   <tt>into</tt> motive, the goal, and the scrutinee, so that the
--   eliminator choice and the later motive construction read from the same
--   decision instead of re-deriving it in two places.
data MatchPlan (n :: S)

-- | <tt>rec-D</tt>: a non-dependent family, so the motive has no scrutinee
--   binder.
MatchRec :: MatchPlan (n :: S)

-- | <tt>ind-D</tt>; the name, when present, is the variable scrutinee to
--   abstract out of the goal.
MatchInd :: Maybe (Name n) -> MatchPlan (n :: S)

-- | Elaborate a match into an application of its datatype's induction
--   eliminator: <tt>ind-D params motive method₁ … methodₖ indices
--   scrutinee</tt>. The spine is the result — a match node never survives
--   elaboration (see the ι-rule in <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.Eval</a> for how the
--   spine then computes).
--   
--   The motive is the elaborated <tt>into</tt> term when one was written;
--   otherwise it is built from the goal, abstracting a variable scrutinee
--   out of it (a non-variable scrutinee gives a constant family). Without
--   <tt>into</tt> and without a goal (inference position) the match is
--   rejected.
checkMatch :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Term n -> Term n -> Maybe (Term n) -> [(VarIdent, Term n)] -> Maybe (TermT n) -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | Check a branch's arm chain against its method type, one arm at a time,
--   mirroring the λ rule: each arm's binder enters the context with the
--   domain of the method's Π-type, and the elaborated arm becomes the
--   method's λ under the same binder. Holes inside the branch body
--   therefore see the branch binders as ordinary hypotheses, under the
--   user's names.
checkMatchArms :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Term n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | β-reduce the administrative redexes elaboration introduces: a motive
--   built as a λ-chain and applied to a constructor form is substituted
--   through, so a branch hole's goal reads as the goal at that constructor
--   (<tt>nat</tt>, or the substituted dependent goal) rather than as
--   <tt>(λ x → …) (suc k)</tt>. This is the labelled-goal restoration of
--   the design: nothing else is unfolded — a motive that is a named family
--   stays a named application.
betaMotiveApps :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | The number of arms in a branch's chain (the binders the branch
--   introduces).
armCount :: forall (x :: S). Term x -> Int

-- | The first name occurring twice, if any.
firstDuplicate :: [VarIdent] -> Maybe VarIdent

-- | A motive built from the goal: λ-binders along the motive's Π-type (the
--   family's indices, then the scrutinee), whose body is the goal — with
--   the scrutinee variable replaced by the motive's own scrutinee binder,
--   when the scrutinee is a variable. A non-variable scrutinee gives a
--   constant family. (The motive types the eliminator generator builds are
--   literal Π-chains, so matching them structurally is enough; cf.
--   <a>lambdaHoleOf</a>.)
motiveFromGoal :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> TermT n -> Maybe (Name n) -> TermT n -> TermT n
inferAs :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> Term n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)
infer :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Term n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)

-- | The type of the motive of a path induction: <tt>(z : A) → (a =_A z) →
--   U</tt>.
motiveType :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n (TermT n)
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Judgements.ElimCost
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.TypeCheck.Judgements.ElimCost


-- | Declarations, sections, commands, and the public entry points.
--   
--   A top-level entry is a name bound in the outermost scope, so the scope
--   <i>grows</i> as a module is checked: each <tt>#define</tt>,
--   <tt>#postulate</tt> and <tt>#assume</tt> enters a binder and the rest
--   of the module is checked under it. The driver is therefore written in
--   continuation-passing style, and the result is packaged with the scope
--   it was produced in (<a>Checked</a>).
--   
--   That also gives sections their shape. A <tt>#assume</tt>d assumption
--   is an ordinary binder, and closing the section abstracts it out of the
--   definitions that used it (<tt>makeAssumptionExplicit</tt>), rewriting
--   the later definitions to apply them to it.
module Rzk.TypeCheck.Decl
data Decl (n :: S)
Decl :: VarIdent -> Name n -> TermT n -> Maybe (TermT n) -> Bool -> [Name n] -> Maybe LocationInfo -> Decl (n :: S)

-- | the surface name, as the user wrote it (with its source position)
[declName] :: Decl (n :: S) -> VarIdent

-- | the name it is bound to in the top-level scope
[declNameOf] :: Decl (n :: S) -> Name n
[declType] :: Decl (n :: S) -> TermT n
[declValue] :: Decl (n :: S) -> Maybe (TermT n)
[declIsAssumption] :: Decl (n :: S) -> Bool
[declUsedVars] :: Decl (n :: S) -> [Name n]
[declLocation] :: Decl (n :: S) -> Maybe LocationInfo
sinkDecl :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). DExt n l => Decl n -> Decl l

-- | Sinking a whole list is a coercion too, with no per-element rebuild.
sinkDecls :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). DExt n l => [Decl n] -> [Decl l]

-- | The per-file groups also sink by coercion. <a>sink1</a> cannot see
--   through the pair (its element must be the sunk type itself), but the
--   sinkability argument is the same: only the declarations mention the
--   scope.
sinkDeclGroups :: forall (n :: S) (l :: S). DExt n l => [(FilePath, [Decl n])] -> [(FilePath, [Decl l])]

-- | What a run of the checker produced: the top-level scope, the
--   declarations in it, and the errors found.
--   
--   The scope is existential, and the declarations live in it. Anything
--   that wants to <i>resume</i> from a checked prefix (the LSP's
--   incremental path) keeps the whole package and carries on from that
--   context; anything that only displays them reads them through the
--   context's naming.
data Checked
