[Checked] :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Context n -> [(FilePath, [Decl n])] -> [TypeErrorInScopedContext] -> [CheckWarning] -> Checked

-- | Bind a top-level entry and run the rest of the module under it.
withTopLevel :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => VarIdent -> TermT n -> Maybe (TermT n) -> Bool -> [Name n] -> Maybe (DataRole n) -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => NameBinder n l -> Decl l -> TypeCheck l r) -> TypeCheck n r

-- | Record a new entry in the innermost open section.
recordInSection :: forall (n :: S). Name n -> Context n -> Context n
startSection :: forall (n :: S) a. Maybe SectionName -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a

-- | Close a section: abstract each of its assumptions out of the
--   definitions that used it, report the ones that went unused, and take
--   the assumptions back out of scope.
--   
--   The definitions stay in scope, with their entries rewritten to take
--   the assumption as an explicit parameter. The assumptions' names stay
--   in the /scope index/ — a scope only ever grows — but they are removed
--   from the surface-name map and from the list of what is in scope, so
--   they can no longer be referred to, shown, or shadowed.
endSection :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [TypeErrorInScopedContext] -> TypeCheck n ([Decl n], [TypeErrorInScopedContext], Context n)

-- | An error, captured in the current context (rather than thrown).
typeErrorHere :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TypeError n -> TypeCheck n TypeErrorInScopedContext

-- | Turn the section's entries into declarations, abstracting each
--   assumption out of the definitions that follow it.
--   
--   The entries come newest first, so the definitions accumulated in
--   <tt>recent</tt> are exactly those that could have used the assumption
--   currently being processed.
collectSectionDecls :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Bool -> [TypeErrorInScopedContext] -> [(Name n, VarInfo n)] -> [(Name n, VarInfo n)] -> TypeCheck n ([(Name n, VarInfo n)], [TypeErrorInScopedContext])

-- | Abstract one assumption out of the definitions that come after it.
--   
--   A definition that mentions the assumption gains it as an explicit
--   parameter, and every later definition that mentions <i>that</i>
--   definition is rewritten to apply it to the assumption. A definition
--   that mentions it without declaring it in its <tt>uses</tt> clause is
--   an implicit assumption, and an error. | Whether an assumption was
--   taken up by (abstracted into) any definition that followed it in its
--   section.
data AssumptionUse
AssumptionUsed :: AssumptionUse
AssumptionUnused :: AssumptionUse
makeAssumptionExplicit :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => (Name n, VarInfo n) -> [(Name n, VarInfo n)] -> TypeCheck n (AssumptionUse, [(Name n, VarInfo n)])

-- | Give an entry the assumption as an explicit parameter.
abstractOver :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> Name n -> VarInfo n -> VarInfo n -> VarInfo n

-- | Rewrite every use of a definition into an application of it to the
--   assumption it has just been abstracted over.
applyToAssumption :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Scope n -> Name n -> (Name n, VarInfo n) -> VarInfo n -> VarInfo n
countCommands :: Integral a => [Command] -> a
setOption :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => String -> String -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a
unsetOption :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => String -> TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n a
paramToParamDecl :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Param -> TypeCheck n [ParamDecl]
addParams :: [Param] -> Term -> Term

-- | The index telescope of the sort. The sort must be <tt>U</tt> (no
--   indices) or a Π-telescope of plain types ending in <tt>U</tt>.
dataSortIndices :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => DataSort -> TypeCheck n [SortIndex]
dataBodyParts :: DataBody -> ([Constructor], [DataElim])

-- | The parameters of a <tt>#data</tt> must be plain typed variables
--   <tt>(x : A)</tt>: the constructors and eliminators apply the type
--   former to them.
dataParamVars :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => [Param] -> TypeCheck n [VarIdent]

-- | A constructor field: a typed parameter, with cube/shape fields
--   rejected (over a directed interval they would declare directed cells,
--   out of scope for M3) and modal fields deferred (crisp induction).
dataFieldToParamDecl :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => VarIdent -> Param -> TypeCheck n [ParamDecl]
modalFieldError :: forall (n :: S) a. Distinct n => VarIdent -> TypeCheck n a
dataConSurface :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => VarIdent -> [VarIdent] -> [ParamDecl] -> Int -> Constructor -> TypeCheck n DataConSurface

-- | The assumptions an entry depends on, possibly only through the types
--   of what it mentions. The generated entries of a <tt>#data</tt> declare
--   these dependencies, so that closing a section abstracts the assumption
--   over all of them uniformly instead of reporting an implicit
--   assumption.
assumptionDepsOf :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> TypeCheck n [Name n]

-- | Several distinct fresh identifiers with a shared base.
freshIdents :: forall (n :: S). Int -> [VarIdentToken] -> Text -> TypeCheck n [VarIdent]

-- | An identifier that is neither bound at the top level nor among the
--   given local binder tokens; primes are appended until one is free. Used
--   for the motive and scrutinee binders of the generated eliminator
--   types, which close over the user's field types.
freshIdent :: forall (n :: S). Maybe FilePath -> [VarIdentToken] -> Text -> TypeCheck n VarIdent

-- | Bind the products of one <tt>#data</tt> declaration: the type former,
--   the constructors (checked in a scope where the type former exists),
--   and the generated eliminators <tt>ind-D</tt> and <tt>rec-D</tt>.
withDataDecls :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => Maybe FilePath -> [Name n] -> VarIdent -> [VarIdent] -> [ParamDecl] -> [SortIndex] -> [DataConSurface] -> [DataElim] -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => [Decl l] -> TypeCheck l r) -> TypeCheck n r

-- | Run a command, recording which one it is and where.
--   
--   An error raised anywhere in the command (or in the rest of the module,
--   which is checked inside it) is <i>collected</i> rather than thrown:
--   the declarations made before it stand, the error is reported, and the
--   rest of the module is skipped. The strict entry points turn the first
--   collected error back into a thrown one.
withCommand :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => Command -> ([Decl n] -> [TypeErrorInScopedContext] -> TypeCheck n r) -> TypeCheck n r -> TypeCheck n r

-- | The binder leaves repeated within one binder <i>group</i> of a surface
--   command: the parameter list of a λ, of a declaration, or of a
--   constructor (a single pattern's leaves are part of their group). Each
--   hit pairs the repeated occurrence with the earlier ones it clashes
--   with.
--   
--   Shadowing an outer binder stays a warning (<a>checkNameShadowing</a>);
--   a duplicate inside one group can only be a mistake, and the silent
--   freshening it used to get showed names the user never wrote (issue
--   #321).
duplicateBinders :: Data a => a -> [(VarIdent, [VarIdent])]

-- | Report a command's error and go on to the next one, with the command
--   itself contributing nothing to the scope.
--   
--   This is the recovery for a command that cannot be stood in for: a
--   declaration whose <i>type</i> does not check has no type to enter it
--   at. The uses of it below then report an undefined variable, which is
--   noisier than the one error but keeps the rest of the file's own errors
--   and holes visible, which is what a file being edited is wanted for.
skippingCommand :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => TypeErrorInScopedContext -> Maybe FilePath -> Integer -> Integer -> [Command] -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => [Decl l] -> [TypeErrorInScopedContext] -> TypeCheck l r) -> TypeCheck n r

-- | Run a check, handing back its error instead of propagating it.
--   
--   What it recorded on the way is kept: the record lives in the state
--   beneath the error channel, so the holes the user wrote in a definition
--   that fails are still reported (see <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.Monad</a>).
tryCheck :: forall (n :: S) a. TypeCheck n a -> TypeCheck n (Either TypeErrorInScopedContext a)

-- | Run a check with the location narrowed to where a surface term was
--   written.
--   
--   Descending through a judgement already narrows to the sub-term it is
--   about (<tt>narrowLocation</tt> in <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.Monad</a>), but
--   only a <i>node</i> carries a position: a variable is a leaf of the
--   core syntax, with nowhere to put one. So a check that starts from a
--   surface term says where that term starts, and a definition whose body
--   is a bare variable is reported at the body rather than at the
--   declaration above it.
atSurface :: forall a (n :: S) b. HasPosition a => a -> TypeCheck n b -> TypeCheck n b

-- | Elaborate a surface term in the current top-level scope: a free
--   identifier resolves to the top-level entry it names.
elaborate :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Term -> TypeCheck n (Term n)

-- | Is a surface identifier defined at the top level?
checkDefined :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => VarIdent -> TypeCheck n (Name n)
splitSectionCommands :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => SectionName -> [Command] -> TypeCheck n ([Command], [Command])

-- | Check a module's commands, extending the scope with each definition.
--   
--   The continuation runs in the <i>final</i> scope, with the declarations
--   the module produced (sunk into it) and the errors found.
checkCommands :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => Maybe FilePath -> Integer -> Integer -> [Command] -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => [Decl l] -> [TypeErrorInScopedContext] -> TypeCheck l r) -> TypeCheck n r

-- | Assume a list of names of the same type, each a top-level entry.
assume :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => [VarIdent] -> TermT n -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => [Decl l] -> TypeCheck l r) -> TypeCheck n r

-- | Check the commands of a section, then close it.
withSection :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => Maybe SectionName -> Integer -> [Command] -> Maybe FilePath -> Integer -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => [Decl l] -> [TypeErrorInScopedContext] -> TypeCheck l r) -> TypeCheck n r

-- | Check one module.
checkModule :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => Maybe FilePath -> Module -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => [Decl l] -> [TypeErrorInScopedContext] -> TypeCheck l r) -> TypeCheck n r
checkModuleWithLocation :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => (FilePath, Module) -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => [Decl l] -> [TypeErrorInScopedContext] -> TypeCheck l r) -> TypeCheck n r

-- | Check a list of modules, one after another, in a scope that grows as
--   it goes.
--   
--   Checking stops at the first module with an error, as it did before.
checkModules :: forall (n :: S) r. Distinct n => [(FilePath, Module)] -> (forall (l :: S). (DExt n l, Distinct l) => [(FilePath, [Decl l])] -> [TypeErrorInScopedContext] -> TypeCheck l r) -> TypeCheck n r

-- | Check the modules, and package the result with the scope it was
--   checked in. The warnings are recorded during the run and are folded
--   into the <a>Checked</a> package here.
checkedModules :: [(FilePath, Module)] -> Context 'VoidS -> Either TypeErrorInScopedContext (Checked, [HoleInfo])

-- | Check the modules strictly: an unfilled hole is an error, and the
--   first error stops the run.
typecheckModules :: [(FilePath, Module)] -> Either TypeErrorInScopedContext Checked

-- | Check the modules in lenient hole mode, returning the holes recorded
--   (each with its goal and local context). This is the structured
--   goal/context query the LSP and the game consume.
typecheckModulesWithHoles :: [(FilePath, Module)] -> Either TypeErrorInScopedContext (Checked, [HoleInfo])

-- | Like <a>typecheckModulesWithHoles</a>, but additionally offers the
--   given named top-level definitions as hole candidates (each applied to
--   holes when its type fits the goal, and never below its meta prefix —
--   an unsaturated schema is not a suggestion, see
--   <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.MetaPrefix</a>). The game passes a level's allow-list
--   of relevant lemmas so they surface as moves; an empty list reproduces
--   <a>typecheckModulesWithHoles</a>.
typecheckModulesWithHolesAndLemmas :: [VarIdent] -> [(FilePath, Module)] -> Either TypeErrorInScopedContext (Checked, [HoleInfo])

-- | A declaration, rendered: no scope index, and nothing to re-elaborate.
--   
--   This is what the LSP shows — a name, a type, a location — and it is
--   all it needs. The elaborated terms stay inside the <a>Checked</a>
--   package, which is what a <i>resume</i> needs.
data DeclView
DeclView :: VarIdent -> Rendered -> Bool -> Maybe LocationInfo -> DeclKind -> DeclView
[declViewName] :: DeclView -> VarIdent
[declViewType] :: DeclView -> Rendered
[declViewIsAssumption] :: DeclView -> Bool
[declViewLocation] :: DeclView -> Maybe LocationInfo
[declViewKind] :: DeclView -> DeclKind

-- | What kind of declaration a <a>DeclView</a> renders: a plain
--   definition, a postulate, or one of the products of a <tt>#data</tt>
--   (the symbol providers group constructors under their type and keep the
--   generated eliminators out of the outline; the semantic tokens
--   highlight postulates distinctly).
data DeclKind
DeclKindDefine :: DeclKind

-- | a <tt>#postulate</tt> or <tt>#assume</tt>: declared, but not proven
DeclKindPostulate :: DeclKind
DeclKindData :: DeclKind

-- | a constructor of the named type
DeclKindDataCon :: VarIdent -> DeclKind

-- | a generated eliminator of the named type
DeclKindDataElim :: VarIdent -> DeclKind

-- | The declarations of a checked run, rendered, grouped by the file they
--   came from.
declViews :: Checked -> [(FilePath, [DeclView])]

-- | Continue checking from a prefix that has already been checked.
--   
--   This is the incremental path: the cached context <i>is</i> the
--   elaborated prefix, so nothing is replayed and nothing is
--   re-elaborated.
recheckFrom :: Checked -> [(FilePath, Module)] -> Either TypeErrorInScopedContext (Checked, [HoleInfo])

-- | The errors of a checked run.
checkedErrors :: Checked -> [TypeErrorInScopedContext]

-- | The warnings of a checked run.
checkedWarnings :: Checked -> [CheckWarning]

-- | Nothing checked yet: the empty context, and no declarations.
emptyChecked :: Checked

-- | Nothing checked yet, in lenient hole mode: what an editor resumes
--   from.
--   
--   A hole is work in progress there, to be reported with its goal and
--   context rather than as an error (see <a>allowHoles</a>).
--   <a>recheckFrom</a> continues in the context it is given, so the mode
--   has to be set on the empty one it starts with: resuming from
--   <a>emptyChecked</a> made every hole a <tt>TypeErrorUnsolvedHole</tt>
--   and stopped the file at the first one.
emptyCheckedWithHoles :: Checked
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Decl.DeclKind
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.Decl.DeclView
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.TypeCheck.Decl.DeclKind
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.TypeCheck.Decl.DeclView
instance Control.Monad.Foil.Internal.Sinkable Rzk.TypeCheck.Decl.Decl


-- | The elaborated types of a declaration's local binders, for LSP hover.
--   
--   Every node of a typed term carries its type, so even a bare λ's binder
--   is typed — by the domain of the λ's own Π-type.
--   
--   The old version threaded a <tt>BinderNames</tt> environment down
--   through the term, to say what each variable it met was called. There
--   is no need: entering a binder puts it in the context, and the context
--   already knows what everything in it is called (see
--   <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.Display</a>).
module Rzk.TypeCheck.BinderTypes

-- | A binder's displayed type: a plain type, or a cube together with a
--   tope, for a shaped binder like <tt>(t : I | φ t)</tt>.
data BinderTypeView
TypeView :: Rendered -> BinderTypeView
ShapeView :: Rendered -> Rendered -> BinderTypeView

-- | Render a term with the names of the context it is in.
renderHere :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> TypeCheck n Rendered

-- | The memoised weak head normal form of a typed term, if present.
memoWHNF :: forall (n :: S). TermT n -> TermT n

-- | The variables a binder introduces, with their rendered types.
--   
--   A pair binder splits its type along Σ-types and cube products; when
--   the shape is not syntactic (the type is a defined name applied to
--   arguments, as in <tt>((η , (ϵ , (α , β))) : has-quasi-diagrammatic-adj
--   A B f u)</tt>), the type is put in weak head normal form first, which
--   needs the top-level definitions in scope. The dependent part is
--   rendered under the earlier component's display name, giving <tt>q : B
--   p</tt>.
binderTypeEntries :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Binder -> TermT n -> TypeCheck n [(VarIdent, BinderTypeView)]

-- | View a type as a Σ-type or a cube product: syntactically, or through
--   the memoised WHNF if possible, computing the WHNF otherwise. Never
--   throws.
splitViewM :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n (Maybe (TermT n))

-- | The elaborated types of the local binders of a typed term, keyed by
--   the binder's original identifier (whose position points at its
--   defining occurrence).
binderTypesOfTerm :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => TermT n -> TypeCheck n [(VarIdent, BinderTypeView)]

-- | All the local binder types of a declaration: Π and Σ binders from its
--   type, λ and let binders from its value.
declBinderTypes :: forall (n :: S). Distinct n => Decl n -> TypeCheck n [(VarIdent, BinderTypeView)]

-- | The elaborated types of the local binders of one file's declarations,
--   with the rest of the run's declarations in scope so that <a>whnfT</a>
--   can unfold definitions when splitting pair binders.
--   
--   Pure at the interface: it runs the checker silently and returns no
--   entries where it fails.
binderTypesOfFile :: Checked -> FilePath -> [(VarIdent, BinderTypeView)]
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.TypeCheck.BinderTypes.BinderTypeView
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.TypeCheck.BinderTypes.BinderTypeView


-- | The type checker.
--   
--   This module is the public face of it: the judgements themselves live
--   in <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.Judgements</a>, the module driver and the
--   declarations in <a>Rzk.TypeCheck.Decl</a>, and so on. What used to be
--   one 5,500-line module is now a layer per concern, over the free-foil
--   core in <a>Language.Rzk.Foil.Syntax</a>.
module Rzk.TypeCheck

module Rzk.Main
parseStdin :: IO Module

-- | Finds matches to the given pattern in the current working directory.
--   **NOTE:** throws exception when <a>glob</a> returns an empty list.
globNonEmpty :: FilePath -> IO [FilePath]
extractFilesFromRzkYaml :: FilePath -> IO [FilePath]

-- | Given a list of file paths (possibly including globs), expands the
--   globs (if any) or tries to read the list of files from the rzk.yaml
--   file (if no paths are given). Glob patterns in rzk.yaml are also
--   expanded.
expandRzkPathsOrYaml :: [FilePath] -> IO [FilePath]
parseRzkFilesOrStdin :: [FilePath] -> IO [(FilePath, Module)]
typecheckString :: Text -> Either Text Text


-- | Structured diagnostics for rzk: type errors and holes as data
--   (severity, a stable code, a source location, and a message) rather
--   than a single pre-formatted string. The core library produces these;
--   the LSP maps them to LSP diagnostics, and the CLI can emit them as
--   JSON (<tt>rzk typecheck --json</tt>).
--   
--   Locations are line-level: rzk currently retains only file + line at
--   the point an error is produced (the column is discarded, and core
--   terms keep no per-node position), so diagnostics point at the
--   enclosing command's line.
module Rzk.Diagnostic

-- | Diagnostic severity, mirroring the usual LSP levels.
data Severity
SeverityError :: Severity
SeverityWarning :: Severity
SeverityInformation :: Severity
SeverityHint :: Severity

-- | A structured diagnostic. Independent of any editor protocol: the LSP
--   maps it to its own <tt>Diagnostic</tt>, and the CLI serialises it as
--   JSON.
--   
--   <h2>JSON wire format (<tt>rzk typecheck --json</tt>)</h2>
--   
--   This is a stable format that downstream tools (e.g. richer LSP hovers)
--   pin to. Each diagnostic is an object:
--   
--   <pre>
--   { "severity": "error" | "warning" | "information" | "hint"
--   , "code":     &lt;string&gt;           -- "hole", or a TypeError tag (e.g. "TypeErrorUnify")
--   , "location": { "file": &lt;string|null&gt;, "line": &lt;int|null&gt; } | null
--   , "message":  &lt;string&gt;           -- human-facing prose (the CLI/LSP display text)
--   , "hole":     &lt;HoleData&gt; | null  -- present only for hole diagnostics (see 'HoleData')
--   }
--   </pre>
--   
--   The <tt>message</tt> field is kept for back-compat (the LSP and the
--   CLI human mode use it). Structured consumers should read the
--   <tt>hole</tt> object instead of parsing <tt>message</tt>. For non-hole
--   diagnostics <tt>hole</tt> is <tt>null</tt>.
data Diagnostic
Diagnostic :: Severity -> String -> Maybe LocationInfo -> String -> Maybe HoleData -> Diagnostic
[diagnosticSeverity] :: Diagnostic -> Severity

-- | stable category, e.g. <tt>"TypeErrorUnify"</tt> or <tt>"hole"</tt>
[diagnosticCode] :: Diagnostic -> String

-- | file + line (line-level granularity)
[diagnosticLocation] :: Diagnostic -> Maybe LocationInfo
[diagnosticMessage] :: Diagnostic -> String

-- | structured hole payload (<a>Nothing</a> for type errors)
[diagnosticHole] :: Diagnostic -> Maybe HoleData

-- | The structured payload of a hole diagnostic: the goal and local
--   context as already-rendered display strings (the same strings the
--   LSP/CLI show, i.e. <tt>show</tt> = <tt>printTree</tt> on the
--   underlying terms). Consumers render hole panels from these fields
--   directly, without parsing the human-facing <tt>message</tt>.
--   
--   <h2>JSON wire format</h2>
--   
--   <pre>
--   { "name":     &lt;string|null&gt;                 -- the ?name, if the hole was named
--   , "goal":     &lt;string&gt;                       -- the expected type (the goal)
--   , "shape":    { "binder": &lt;string&gt;, "tope": &lt;string&gt; } | null
--   , "termVars": [ { "name": &lt;string&gt;, "type": &lt;string&gt; }, ... ]
--   , "cubeVars": [ { "name": &lt;string&gt;, "type": &lt;string&gt; }, ... ]
--   , "topes":    [ &lt;string&gt;, ... ]              -- local tope assumptions (excludes ⊤)
--   }
--   </pre>
--   
--   Notes for consumers:
--   
--   <ul>
--   <li><tt>shape</tt> is non-null only for a shape-restricted
--   <i>argument</i> goal, where the goal reads <tt>(binder : goal |
--   tope)</tt>. For an <i>extension</i> type the boundary is already part
--   of <tt>goal</tt> (a restricted type <tt>A [ … ↦ … ]</tt>), and
--   <tt>shape</tt> is <tt>null</tt> — read the boundary out of
--   <tt>goal</tt>.</li>
--   <li><tt>cubeVars</tt> names can be patterns like <tt>"(t, s)"</tt>
--   (pair-pattern binders); they are display strings, not single
--   identifiers.</li>
--   </ul>
data HoleData
HoleData :: Maybe String -> String -> Maybe (String, String) -> [(String, String)] -> [(String, String)] -> [String] -> HoleData

-- | the <tt>?name</tt>, if named
[holeDataName] :: HoleData -> Maybe String

-- | the goal (expected type)
[holeDataGoal] :: HoleData -> String

-- | (binder, tope) for a shape-argument goal
[holeDataShape] :: HoleData -> Maybe (String, String)

-- | local hypotheses: (name, type)
[holeDataTermVars] :: HoleData -> [(String, String)]

-- | local cube variables: (name, type)
[holeDataCubeVars] :: HoleData -> [(String, String)]

-- | local tope assumptions (excluding ⊤)
[holeDataTopes] :: HoleData -> [String]

-- | Encode a location as JSON. A plain helper rather than a
--   <tt>ToJSON</tt> instance, to avoid an orphan instance
--   (<a>LocationInfo</a> is defined in <a>Rzk.TypeCheck</a>).
locationToJSON :: LocationInfo -> Value

-- | A stable tag for a type error, used as its diagnostic code.
--   Independent of the variable type, so it survives the scoped-error
--   unfolding.
typeErrorTag :: forall (n :: S). TypeError n -> String

-- | The tag of a type error.
--   
--   An error carries the context it was raised in, so there are no binder
--   layers to peel: the old representation nested the error one Inc deeper
--   at every binder.
typeErrorTagInScopedContext :: TypeErrorInScopedContext -> String

-- | The source location of a type error (the enclosing command's line).
locationOfTypeError :: TypeErrorInScopedContext -> Maybe LocationInfo

-- | A structured diagnostic for a type error. The message is the usual
--   formatted error text; severity is always <a>SeverityError</a>.
diagnoseTypeError :: OutputDirection -> TypeErrorInScopedContext -> Diagnostic

-- | A checker warning as a diagnostic: warning severity, with the
--   warning's constructor name as the stable code (like
--   <a>diagnoseTypeError</a> does for errors).
diagnoseCheckWarning :: CheckWarning -> Diagnostic

-- | A checker warning as a human-readable line (the CLI).
ppCheckWarning :: CheckWarning -> String

-- | The stable tag of a warning (its diagnostic code), used to match
--   <tt>warnings</tt> in fixtures; sharing the definition keeps the two
--   from drifting apart.
checkWarningTag :: CheckWarning -> String

-- | A structured diagnostic for a hole, carrying the hole's goal and local
--   context. A hole is an unfilled obligation, so it is a
--   <a>SeverityWarning</a> — mirroring Agda's yellow "unsolved" highlight,
--   and visible in the editor's problems panel (unlike
--   <a>SeverityHint</a>, which editors render almost invisibly). Finished
--   work still rejects holes outright: the strict default of <tt>rzk
--   typecheck</tt> reports them as errors (cf. Agda's <tt>--safe</tt>).
diagnoseHole :: HoleInfo -> Diagnostic

-- | The structured payload of a hole: its goal and local context rendered
--   to display strings (the same rendering <a>ppHoleInfo</a> uses, but
--   kept as separate fields rather than concatenated into prose). See
--   <a>HoleData</a>.
holeData :: HoleInfo -> HoleData

-- | Render a hole's goal and local context (the structured query) for
--   display, separating term variables, cube variables, and tope
--   assumptions.
ppHoleInfo :: HoleInfo -> String
ppLocationInfo :: LocationInfo -> String
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.Diagnostic.Diagnostic
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.Diagnostic.HoleData
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.Diagnostic.Severity
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.Diagnostic.Diagnostic
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.Diagnostic.HoleData
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.Diagnostic.Severity
instance Data.Aeson.Types.ToJSON.ToJSON Rzk.Diagnostic.Diagnostic
instance Data.Aeson.Types.ToJSON.ToJSON Rzk.Diagnostic.HoleData
instance Data.Aeson.Types.ToJSON.ToJSON Rzk.Diagnostic.Severity

module Language.Rzk.VSCode.Env

-- | What checking one module produced.
--   
--   <a>cachedModuleChecked</a> is the state of the whole run <i>after</i>
--   this module: the top-level scope and every declaration elaborated so
--   far. That is what a resume starts from — a cached elaborated term
--   names the definitions it uses by their foil name, which only means
--   anything in the scope that produced it, so the scope has to be cached
--   with them.
--   
--   <a>cachedModuleDecls</a> is the rendered view of this module's own
--   declarations, which is all that completion, symbols and hover need.
data RzkCachedModule
RzkCachedModule :: Checked -> [DeclView] -> [TypeErrorInScopedContext] -> RzkCachedModule
[cachedModuleChecked] :: RzkCachedModule -> Checked
[cachedModuleDecls] :: RzkCachedModule -> [DeclView]
[cachedModuleErrors] :: RzkCachedModule -> [TypeErrorInScopedContext]
type RzkTypecheckCache = [(FilePath, RzkCachedModule)]

-- | Where a parse came from, deciding whether it may be reused.
data ParseSource

-- | Parsed from the editor buffer with this text; reusable for the current
--   file while the buffer text is unchanged.
ParsedFromBuffer :: Text -> ParseSource

-- | Parsed from the file on disk; trusted until invalidated by a
--   file-change notification.
ParsedFromDisk :: ParseSource

-- | The file changed; must be re-parsed. The module is kept as the last
--   good parse, which hover falls back to while the file fails to parse.
ParseInvalidated :: ParseSource

-- | A parse result for the reference index. A failed parse is a
--   <a>Nothing</a> module and is not retried until the source changes.
data ParsedModule
ParsedModule :: ParseSource -> Maybe Module -> ParsedModule
[parsedSource] :: ParsedModule -> ParseSource
[parsedModule] :: ParsedModule -> Maybe Module
data ReferenceIndexCache
ReferenceIndexCache :: Map FilePath ParsedModule -> Maybe ([FilePath], ReferenceIndex) -> ReferenceIndexCache

-- | Per-file parse cache. Entries parsed from disk are trusted until a
--   file-change notification evicts them (<a>resetCacheForFiles</a>); the
--   entry for the file being edited is revalidated against the editor
--   buffer.
[indexCacheModules] :: ReferenceIndexCache -> Map FilePath ParsedModule

-- | The index last built, with the file set it was built from.
[indexCacheResult] :: ReferenceIndexCache -> Maybe ([FilePath], ReferenceIndex)
emptyReferenceIndexCache :: ReferenceIndexCache
data RzkEnv
RzkEnv :: TVar RzkTypecheckCache -> TVar ReferenceIndexCache -> TVar (Maybe (Async ())) -> RzkEnv
[rzkEnvTypecheckCache] :: RzkEnv -> TVar RzkTypecheckCache
[rzkEnvReferenceIndexCache] :: RzkEnv -> TVar ReferenceIndexCache

-- | The thread running the current project typecheck, if any.
[rzkEnvTypecheckWorker] :: RzkEnv -> TVar (Maybe (Async ()))
defaultRzkEnv :: IO RzkEnv
type LSP = LspT ServerConfig ReaderT RzkEnv IO

-- | Run the given action (a project typecheck) on a fresh worker thread,
--   cancelling the previous worker first. Cancellation waits for the old
--   worker to stop, so it can no longer write to the caches once the new
--   one starts. Typechecking runs on a worker so that the handler dispatch
--   thread stays responsive: <tt>lsp</tt> dispatches messages
--   sequentially, so a multi-second re-check run directly in a
--   notification handler would block every later request (e.g. formatting
--   on save).
spawnTypecheckWorker :: LSP () -> LSP ()
cacheTypecheckedModules :: RzkTypecheckCache -> LSP ()
resetCacheForAllFiles :: LSP ()
resetCacheForFiles :: [FilePath] -> LSP ()
getCachedTypecheckedModules :: LSP RzkTypecheckCache
cacheReferenceIndex :: ReferenceIndexCache -> LSP ()
getCachedReferenceIndex :: LSP ReferenceIndexCache

module Language.Rzk.VSCode.Handlers
typecheckFromConfigFile :: LSP ()
provideCompletions :: Handler LSP 'Method_TextDocumentCompletion
provideSymbols :: Handler LSP 'Method_TextDocumentDocumentSymbol

-- | Workspace-wide symbol search over every typechecked module in the
--   cache. The query is matched case-insensitively as an infix of the
--   definition name; an empty query lists all definitions (clients filter
--   further as the user types).
provideWorkspaceSymbols :: Handler LSP 'Method_WorkspaceSymbol
findDefinition :: Handler LSP 'Method_TextDocumentDefinition
findReferences :: Handler LSP 'Method_TextDocumentReferences
provideHover :: Handler LSP 'Method_TextDocumentHover

-- | A signature for the hover code block. A long function type is split
--   with one parameter per line, in the style rzk definitions are written:
--   
--   <pre>
--   is-equiv
--     : ( A : U)
--     → ( B : U)
--     → ( f : A → B)
--     → U
--   </pre>
formatSignature :: String -> Term -> String
formatDocument :: Handler LSP 'Method_TextDocumentFormatting
provideSemanticTokens :: Handler LSP 'Method_TextDocumentSemanticTokensFull

-- | The checker-derived token overlay for identifier <i>uses</i>: an
--   occurrence that resolves to a product of a <tt>#data</tt> declaration
--   is coloured by its kind wherever it appears — a constructor as an enum
--   member, the type as a class, a generated eliminator as a library
--   function — and an occurrence of a postulate or an assumption is marked
--   abstract (declared, but not proven), so a proof that leans on an axiom
--   is visible at a glance. Postulates, top-level assumptions, and
--   in-section assumptions get distinct type/modifier combinations, in
--   decreasing order of severity. Occurrences are matched to declarations
--   by definition site (file and line) <i>and</i> name, so a local that
--   shadows a constructor stays plain, and plain definitions are left to
--   the lexer baseline. Positions are code points, like every other token
--   source; the UTF-16 conversion happens after merging.
useSiteTokens :: [(FilePath, [DeclView])] -> ReferenceIndex -> FilePath -> [SemanticTokenAbsolute]

-- | The cache eviction and the re-typecheck run on the typecheck worker
--   thread, so this handler returns immediately and later requests (e.g. a
--   formatting request from format-on-save) are answered while the project
--   re-check is still running. Spawning the worker cancels the previous
--   one, so a newer change restarts the re-check.
handleFilesChanged :: Handler LSP 'Method_WorkspaceDidChangeWatchedFiles
instance Data.Default.Internal.Default Language.LSP.Protocol.Internal.Types.CompletionItem.CompletionItem
instance Data.Default.Internal.Default Language.LSP.Protocol.Internal.Types.CompletionItemLabelDetails.CompletionItemLabelDetails
instance Data.Default.Internal.Default Data.Text.Internal.Text

module Language.Rzk.VSCode.Lsp

-- | The maximum number of diagnostic messages to send to the client
maxDiagnosticCount :: Int
handlers :: Handlers LSP
syncOptions :: TextDocumentSyncOptions
runLsp :: IO Int


-- | Which build of rzk this is: the package version, the commit it was
--   built from (when the build supplied one), the compiler and platform,
--   and which Cabal flags it was built with.
--   
--   The package version itself is generated by Cabal into
--   <tt>Paths_rzk</tt>, an autogenerated <i>other</i> module of the
--   library, so a tool that links rzk cannot import it. This module
--   exposes it as part of the public API instead, together with the rest
--   of the build details, so a consumer (the <tt>rzk</tt> executable, the
--   rzk-game) can report which checker it is running.
module Rzk.Version

-- | The version of the <tt>rzk</tt> package.
version :: Version

-- | The version of the <tt>rzk</tt> package, rendered as a string (e.g.
--   <tt>"0.11.2"</tt>).
--   
--   This is what <tt>rzk version</tt> prints, and tools scrape it as such,
--   so it is deliberately just the version and nothing else.
versionString :: String

-- | Everything this build knows about itself.
data VersionInfo
VersionInfo :: Version -> Maybe String -> Maybe String -> String -> String -> [BuildFlag] -> VersionInfo

-- | The package version.
[versionInfoVersion] :: VersionInfo -> Version

-- | The commit rzk was built from, when the build knew one (see
--   <a>buildCommit</a>); <a>Nothing</a> otherwise.
[versionInfoCommit] :: VersionInfo -> Maybe String

-- | The date of that commit, when it came from a repository (see
--   <a>buildCommitDate</a>).
[versionInfoCommitDate] :: VersionInfo -> Maybe String

-- | The Haskell implementation, e.g. <tt>"ghc-9.10.3"</tt>.
[versionInfoCompiler] :: VersionInfo -> String

-- | Operating system and architecture, e.g. <tt>"darwin-aarch64"</tt>.
[versionInfoPlatform] :: VersionInfo -> String

-- | The Cabal flags this build was made with (see <a>buildFlags</a>).
[versionInfoFlags] :: VersionInfo -> [BuildFlag]

-- | A Cabal flag of the <tt>rzk</tt> package, with the state this build
--   has.
data BuildFlag
BuildFlag :: String -> FlagState -> BuildFlag
[buildFlagName] :: BuildFlag -> String
[buildFlagState] :: BuildFlag -> FlagState

-- | Whether a Cabal flag is on for this build.
data FlagState
FlagOn :: FlagState
FlagOff :: FlagState

-- | The build description of the running rzk.
versionInfo :: VersionInfo

-- | Every Cabal flag of the package, each with the state this build has.
--   
--   A tool that wants a language server can look up <tt>lsp</tt> here
--   rather than run <tt>rzk lsp</tt> and see whether it fails.
--   
--   Note that the state is what was compiled in, not what was asked for:
--   the JavaScript and WebAssembly backends have no LSP support whatever
--   the <tt>lsp</tt> flag says, and <tt>lsp</tt> reads as off in such a
--   build.
buildFlags :: [BuildFlag]

-- | Render a build description as a block of lines, as printed by <tt>rzk
--   version --full</tt>.
ppVersionInfo :: VersionInfo -> String

-- | Git's default commit date (<tt>Fri Aug 21 21:14:42 2026 +0300</tt>) as
--   a plain ISO date (<tt>2026-08-21</tt>), which is the form <tt>rustc
--   -vV</tt> reports. A date that does not parse is passed through
--   unchanged.
isoCommitDate :: String -> String
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.Version.BuildFlag
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.Version.FlagState
instance GHC.Classes.Eq Rzk.Version.VersionInfo
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.Version.BuildFlag
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.Version.FlagState
instance GHC.Internal.Show.Show Rzk.Version.VersionInfo
instance Data.Aeson.Types.ToJSON.ToJSON Rzk.Version.BuildFlag
instance Data.Aeson.Types.ToJSON.ToJSON Rzk.Version.FlagState
instance Data.Aeson.Types.ToJSON.ToJSON Rzk.Version.VersionInfo
